treeskel.segment

Segment the main branches in the summer photo, trained on the hand masks and scored against winter.

The angle CNN of treeskel.shape_cnn learned ten numbers per tree and overfitted (training loss 0.12, held-out 0.7–0.8); the hand masks, a person's reading of the same photos, predict the winter shape far better (skill +0.87 on the V opening against +0.16). The hand masks are in the summer view and have the winter shape (448 of 448 laid onto their winter traces within 8 px). So here a network learns the masks themselves, pixel by pixel, and its predicted masks are measured with the same code as the hand masks (treeskel.shape.mask_branches(), treeskel.shape.shape_measures()).

What changed (the student's decision, session 11): the hand masks of the development rows are now training labels, not only a validation reference. The winter traces stay fully independent: they never train or choose anything here, and the predicted shape is scored against them. The test rows' masks stay unused until the final evaluation.

Caveat: the hand masks are not all on the branch. Session 3 found the sample's masks 15–45 px from the visible summer trunk. On the 21 development trees in the repository (session 11, by eye) most sit on the trunk or within about its width, but several are 20–60 px off to either side, and R20N06's about 90 px (on the winter position, session 7). So the network learns the drawn masks, offsets included (unless they are lined up first, --mask-overlay). The pixel scores against the hand masks mix its error with theirs and are not directly comparable with Chen et al.'s. The shape measures do not depend on where a mask sits, so the headline score against the winter traces is unaffected.

The network (UNet): a U-Net whose encoder is ResNet-18, pretrained on ImageNet (Chen et al. (2020) used ResNet-34, --encoder resnet34), and whose decoder upsamples by two five times, joining the encoder's features at each scale. It sees the masks' frame: the centre 480x480 of the photo, resized to size x size (256, the masks' own resolution, by default).

Full size (--size 480 640, session 12, the one variant agreed at the end of session 11): the whole photo at its own resolution, as the angle CNN's best run. The hand masks cover only the photo's centre 480 columns, so the side columns are unknown to the loss (known_columns(), seg_loss()), and the predictions are measured in the masks' frame (to_mask_size()), exactly as the square runs'. The rotation of the augmentation is made in pixels, so it keeps angles in the wider frame.

Loss (seg_loss()): binary cross-entropy plus the soft Dice loss; branch pixels are only about 6% of the frame, and the Dice term keeps the thin leaders from being traded for background.

Centre-line loss (--cldice, session 16, the student's first candidate for completing leaders): a small break in a thin leader costs few pixels but loses the leader's angles. Shit et al.'s (2021) soft clDice (soft_cldice_loss()) compares the masks' soft centre lines (soft_skeleton()) instead: the loss becomes BCE + (1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice (CLDICE_WEIGHT, CL_ITERS). It may also reward joining the wrong branches, so its runs are scored on side branches too (treeskel.seg_compare). Session 12 used clDice only to choose a threshold for growing finished masks; here it trains the network.

Augmentation (augment_pair()): as for the angle CNN, a random crop of 80–100% of the area, the mirror image half of the time and colour jitter; here also a rotation of up to ±10° (the camera's roll between rows reaches a few degrees). The mask is resampled with the photo, so it stays on the branch. A prediction averages the photo's and its mirror image's probabilities (predict_masks()).

Validation (cross_validate_seg()): the 5 row-grouped folds of splits.json, as treeskel.shape_cnn.cross_validate_cnn(): the number of epochs is chosen on the next fold's rows inside the training rows (their loss against the hand masks), the network is trained again on all training rows, and it predicts the fold's own rows. The recipe (SegParams) was fixed before any result.

Scores (main()), for every development tree from the fold that held its row out:

  • the predicted mask against the hand mask: IoU, Dice, precision, recall (mask_scores(); comparable with Chen et al.'s pixel scores);
  • the shape of the predicted mask against the winter traces, with the skill over the mean shape as in treeskel.shape_model. A predicted mask in which no fork is found counts as the mean shape (the fold's training mean), so failures are not dropped from the score; their number is reported.
  • tree by tree against the angle CNN's runs and, for a run on lined-up masks, the run on the masks as drawn (compare_with()).

Lined-up masks (--mask-overlay, session 11, the student's choice after the first run): each hand mask moved onto its summer photo with treeskel.annotate_mask. Only trees lined up (and not skipped) train, and the pixel scores are against the lined-up masks. The shape scores need no change: moving a mask does not change its angles.

Joined masks (join_pieces(), joined_run(), session 12, as agreed at the end of session 11): the measuring keeps only a mask's largest piece, so a leader cut off by a few pixels of leaves takes the fork with it (14 of the lined-up run's 449 masks had no fork). Before measuring, pieces within JOIN_GAP (about a trunk's width, fixed from the hand masks' geometry, never tuned on winter) are joined to the largest. Every run is also scored this way, into <run>_joined, and both are reported.

Grown masks (grow_mask(), grown_run(), session 12, the student's idea): where leaves hide a leader, the U-Net's probability often fades below 0.5 before the leader ends, so the mask stops short or breaks. On the lined-up run's joined masks (the named model), 31 of the 444 trees scored on the V opening had a predicted leader shorter than the stretch the angles are fitted over (no winter trace or hand mask has a leader that short), and they carried 33% of the V opening's squared error (33 trees and 47% counting also the 2 masks with no fork, in which a leader is cut off from the trunk). Each mask is grown into the less sure pixels connected to it (hysteresis thresholding), then joined. The lower threshold is the one of GROW_LOWS whose masks best match the lined-up hand masks' centre lines (cl_dice()); the winter traces play no part. Training runs save their probabilities in the masks' frame (probabilities.npz) and write <run>_grown beside <run>_joined. Not adopted: on the re-run it grew every mask (a lower threshold of 0.1 chosen), added side branches, and was no closer to winter on the V opening.

Completed leader lines (complete_measures(), completed_run(), session 12, the student's shape-prior idea): a short leader's line over the whole fitted stretch is predicted from its visible part, by a model fitted on complete leaders cut short on purpose (fit_completion()): over the missing part, lines turn more upright and keep turning the way the visible part does. Fitted per fold on the other folds' trees; never on winter.

Continued leaders (continue_leaders(), continued_run(), session 12, the student's next idea): a short leader is joined to a piece lying on its line further on (within CONTINUE_CONE of its direction at the tip, and within the part of the fitted stretch still missing), and each mask is then cut down to its trunk and two leaders (prune_to_branches()). The settings come from the hand masks and the measures' own stretch, never from winter.

Usage, from the command line:

python -m treeskel.segment data/raw                      # the student's PC (GPU); docs/results/segment/
python -m treeskel.segment data/raw --mask-overlay annotations/mask_overlay.json   # docs/results/segment_lined_up/
python -m treeskel.segment data/raw --mask-overlay annotations/mask_overlay.json --size 480 640
                                                         # docs/results/segment_lined_up_480x640/ (+ _joined/)
python -m treeskel.segment data/raw --depth              # docs/results/segment_depth/
python -m treeskel.segment --replot docs/results/segment # figures only
python -m treeskel.segment --join docs/results/segment_lined_up   # its masks joined: segment_lined_up_joined/
python -m treeskel.segment data/raw --grow docs/results/segment_lined_up_rerun   # grown, threshold chosen again
python -m treeskel.segment --continue docs/results/segment_lined_up_rerun_joined  # leaders continued, pruned
python -m treeskel.segment data/raw --mask-overlay annotations/mask_overlay.json --seed 1 --no-grow
                                                         # another sample: docs/results/segment_lined_up_seed1/
python -m treeskel.segment data/raw --mask-overlay annotations/mask_overlay.json --cldice --no-grow
                                                         # the centre-line loss: segment_lined_up_cldice/

 169CLDICE_WEIGHT = 0.5
 170"""``α`` of the centre-line loss when it is switched on (``--cldice``, session 16): the loss is
 171``BCE + (1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice``, Shit et al.'s (2021) combination ``(1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice`` at their
 172public implementation's default ``α`` = 0.5 (checked in their repository, ``soft_dice_cldice``), with the
 173named recipe's cross-entropy kept. Fixed before any run; not tuned."""
 174
 175CL_ITERS = 25
 176"""Erosions of the soft skeleton (:func:`soft_skeleton`). A branch whose distance transform peaks at ``d``
 177px needs ``d − 1`` erosions, or the centre line of its wide parts is missing (checked on synthetic bars and
 178discs, ``tests/test_segment_cldice.py``), and the loss would then ignore the trunk. The development hand
 179masks' trunk radius at the fork reaches 14.8 mask px (448 trees), their widest point 17.0 on the 21 local
 180development trees (the base of the trunk is drawn wider), 19.0 at the augmentation's largest zoom (1/√0.8).
 18125 leaves room for wider trunks on the trees not in the repository: an erosion past a branch's width adds
 182nothing, so too many cost only time. (The authors' implementation uses 10, for thin vessels.) Fixed before
 183any run."""
 184

 186@dataclass(frozen=True)
 187class SegParams:
 188    """The training recipe, fixed before any result.
 189
 190    Attributes:
 191        size: One number: the side of a square input, the photo's centre
 192            480x480 (the hand masks' frame) resized; 256 is the masks' own
 193            resolution. Two, ``(height, width)``: the whole photo resized,
 194            e.g. ``(480, 640)`` at full size (session 12), where the hand
 195            masks cover only the centre columns and the rest is unknown to
 196            the loss (:func:`known_columns`). Each side must divide by 32.
 197        encoder: ``"resnet18"`` or ``"resnet34"``.
 198        epochs: Most epochs tried when choosing the number of epochs.
 199        batch: Photos per training step.
 200        lr_encoder: Learning rate of the pretrained encoder (AdamW).
 201        lr_decoder: Learning rate of the new decoder.
 202        weight_decay: AdamW's weight decay.
 203        crop: Smallest random crop, as a fraction of the frame's area.
 204        rotate: Largest random rotation, degrees either way.
 205        jitter: Brightness, contrast and saturation are scaled by up to
 206            ``1 ± jitter``.
 207        threshold: Probability above which a pixel is branch.
 208        seed: Random seed (each training run adds its own offset).
 209        depth: Also give the network the summer depth, as a fourth channel.
 210        cldice: Weight ``α`` of the soft centre-line Dice in the loss
 211            (:func:`seg_loss`, session 16): ``BCE + (1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice``.
 212            0, the named recipe, leaves the loss as it was.
 213        cl_iters: Erosions of the soft skeleton (:func:`soft_skeleton`); only
 214            used when ``cldice`` > 0 (:data:`CL_ITERS`).
 215    """
 216
 217    size: int | tuple[int, int] = 256
 218    encoder: str = "resnet18"
 219    epochs: int = 60
 220    batch: int = 8
 221    lr_encoder: float = 1e-4
 222    lr_decoder: float = 1e-3
 223    weight_decay: float = 1e-4
 224    crop: float = 0.8
 225    rotate: float = 10.0
 226    jitter: float = 0.2
 227    threshold: float = 0.5
 228    seed: int = 0
 229    depth: bool = False
 230    cldice: float = 0.0
 231    cl_iters: int = CL_ITERS
 232
 233
 234def whole_photo(params: SegParams) -> bool:
 235    """True if the network sees the whole photo (``size`` is ``(height, width)``), not the masks' square frame.
 236
 237    Args:
 238        params: The settings, as :class:`SegParams`.
 239
 240    Returns:
 241        True for a whole-photo network.
 242    """
 243    return not isinstance(params.size, int)
 244
 245
 246def input_shape(params: SegParams) -> tuple[int, int]:
 247    """``(height, width)`` of the network's input.
 248
 249    Args:
 250        params: The settings, as :class:`SegParams`.
 251
 252    Returns:
 253        ``(height, width)`` in pixels.
 254    """
 255    return (params.size, params.size) if not whole_photo(params) else (int(params.size[0]), int(params.size[1]))
 256
 257
 258def known_columns(width: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
 259    """The columns ``[start, stop)`` of a whole photo resized to ``width`` that the hand masks describe (the
 260    photo's columns 80-559, :data:`treeskel.io.CROP_COLS`); outside them a mask says nothing.
 261
 262    Args:
 263        width: The resized photo's width (px).
 264
 265    Returns:
 266        ``(start, stop)`` column indices.
 267
 268    Example:
 269        >>> known_columns(640), known_columns(320)
 270        ((80, 560), (40, 280))
 271    """
 272    from treeskel.io import CROP_COLS, IMAGE_SHAPE
 273
 274    return round(CROP_COLS[0] * width / IMAGE_SHAPE[1]), round(CROP_COLS[1] * width / IMAGE_SHAPE[1])
 275
 276
 277def known_map(params: SegParams) -> np.ndarray | None:
 278    """``(height, width)`` float32, 1 where the hand masks say something and 0 where they do not; None for the
 279    masks' own square frame, where they describe every pixel.
 280
 281    Args:
 282        params: The settings, as :class:`SegParams`.
 283
 284    Returns:
 285        The weight map, or None.
 286    """
 287    if not whole_photo(params):
 288        return None
 289    h, w = input_shape(params)
 290    out = np.zeros((h, w), np.float32)
 291    a, b = known_columns(w)
 292    out[:, a:b] = 1.0
 293    return out
 294
 295
 296def mask_to_photo(mask: np.ndarray, shape: tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray:
 297    """A 256x256 hand mask placed on the whole photo (:func:`treeskel.io.mask_to_image_frame`, but resized
 298    bilinearly, so soft at the edges as in the square frame) and resized to ``shape`` = ``(height, width)``:
 299    uint8 0-255, zero outside the columns it describes.
 300
 301    Args:
 302        mask: A 256x256 boolean hand mask.
 303        shape: The output's ``(height, width)``.
 304
 305    Returns:
 306        The ``(height, width)`` uint8 mask.
 307    """
 308    from PIL import Image
 309
 310    from treeskel.io import CROP_COLS, IMAGE_SHAPE
 311
 312    side = IMAGE_SHAPE[0]
 313    big = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(np.asarray(mask, bool).astype(np.uint8) * 255).resize((side, side),
 314                                                                                            Image.BILINEAR))
 315    full = np.zeros(IMAGE_SHAPE, np.uint8)
 316    full[:, CROP_COLS[0]:CROP_COLS[1]] = big
 317    if tuple(shape) == IMAGE_SHAPE:
 318        return full
 319    return np.asarray(Image.fromarray(full).resize((shape[1], shape[0]), Image.BILINEAR))
 320
 321
 322# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 323# The network
 324# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 325
 326def _block(cin: int, cout: int):
 327    """Two 3x3 convolutions, each with batch norm and ReLU."""
 328    import torch.nn as nn
 329
 330    return nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(cin, cout, 3, padding=1, bias=False), nn.BatchNorm2d(cout), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
 331                         nn.Conv2d(cout, cout, 3, padding=1, bias=False), nn.BatchNorm2d(cout), nn.ReLU(inplace=True))
 332
 333
 334def make_encoder(name: str = "resnet18", pretrained: bool = True, channels: int = 3):
 335    """A torchvision ResNet (18 or 34) for the encoder; with ``channels=4`` its first convolution takes a
 336    depth channel too, whose weights start as the mean of the colour weights (as
 337    :func:`treeskel.shape_cnn.make_model`).
 338
 339    Args:
 340        name: ``"resnet18"`` or ``"resnet34"``.
 341        pretrained: Load the ImageNet weights.
 342        channels: Input channels: 3 (colour) or 4 (colour and depth).
 343
 344    Returns:
 345        The torchvision ResNet.
 346
 347    Raises:
 348        ValueError: If ``channels`` is not 3 or 4, or ``name`` is not one of the two.
 349    """
 350    import torch
 351    from torchvision import models
 352
 353    if name not in ("resnet18", "resnet34"):
 354        raise ValueError(f"encoder must be resnet18 or resnet34, got {name!r}")
 355    weights = {"resnet18": models.ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1,
 356               "resnet34": models.ResNet34_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1}[name]
 357    net = getattr(models, name)(weights=weights if pretrained else None)
 358    if channels == 4:
 359        old = net.conv1
 360        net.conv1 = torch.nn.Conv2d(4, old.out_channels, old.kernel_size, old.stride, old.padding, bias=False)
 361        with torch.no_grad():
 362            net.conv1.weight[:, :3] = old.weight
 363            net.conv1.weight[:, 3] = old.weight.mean(dim=1)
 364    elif channels != 3:
 365        raise ValueError(f"channels must be 3 or 4, got {channels}")
 366    return net
 367
 368
 369def _unet_class():
 370    """The :class:`UNet` class, built on first use so that importing this module needs no PyTorch."""
 371    import torch
 372    import torch.nn as nn
 373    import torch.nn.functional as F
 374
 375    class _UNet(nn.Module):
 376        """U-Net with a ResNet encoder: features at 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 and 1/32 of the input, and a
 377        decoder that doubles the resolution five times, joining the encoder's features at each scale.
 378        Outputs one logit per pixel (branch or not) at the input's size."""
 379
 380        def __init__(self, encoder: str = "resnet18", pretrained: bool = True, channels: int = 3):
 381            """Take the encoder's layers (for ``channels`` input channels) and build the decoder."""
 382            super().__init__()
 383            net = make_encoder(encoder, pretrained, channels)
 384            self.stem = nn.Sequential(net.conv1, net.bn1, net.relu)          # 1/2, 64
 385            self.pool = net.maxpool
 386            self.enc = nn.ModuleList([net.layer1, net.layer2, net.layer3, net.layer4])   # 1/4 ... 1/32
 387            skips = (256, 128, 64, 64)                                        # layer3, layer2, layer1, stem
 388            outs = (256, 128, 64, 32)
 389            ins = (512,) + outs[:-1]
 390            self.dec = nn.ModuleList([_block(i + s, o) for i, s, o in zip(ins, skips, outs)])
 391            self.last = _block(outs[-1], 16)                                  # back to the input's size
 392            self.head = nn.Conv2d(16, 1, 1)
 393
 394        def forward(self, x):
 395            """``(B, H, W)`` logits for ``(B, C, H, W)`` photos whose sides divide by 32."""
 396            if x.shape[-1] % 32 or x.shape[-2] % 32:
 397                raise ValueError(f"the input's sides must divide by 32, got {tuple(x.shape[-2:])}")
 398            s = self.stem(x)
 399            feats = [s]
 400            e = self.pool(s)
 401            for layer in self.enc:
 402                e = layer(e)
 403                feats.append(e)
 404            d = feats[-1]
 405            for block, skip in zip(self.dec, feats[-2::-1]):
 406                d = F.interpolate(d, size=skip.shape[-2:], mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)
 407                d = block(torch.cat([d, skip], dim=1))
 408            d = F.interpolate(d, size=x.shape[-2:], mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)
 409            return self.head(self.last(d))[:, 0]
 410
 411        def groups(self):
 412            """``(encoder parameters, decoder parameters)``, for their own learning rates."""
 413            enc = list(self.stem.parameters()) + list(self.enc.parameters())
 414            ids = {id(p) for p in enc}
 415            return enc, [p for p in self.parameters() if id(p) not in ids]
 416
 417    return _UNet
 418
 419
 420def UNet(encoder: str = "resnet18", pretrained: bool = True, channels: int = 3):
 421    """A U-Net with a ResNet encoder (see the module docstring); ``pretrained`` loads the ImageNet weights.
 422
 423    The model maps ``(B, channels, H, W)`` normalised images (sides divisible
 424    by 32) to ``(B, H, W)`` logits.
 425
 426    Args:
 427        encoder: ``"resnet18"`` or ``"resnet34"``.
 428        pretrained: Load the encoder's ImageNet weights.
 429        channels: Input channels: 3 (colour) or 4 (colour and depth).
 430
 431    Returns:
 432        The model, a ``torch.nn.Module``.
 433    """
 434    return _unet_class()(encoder, pretrained, channels)
 435
 436
 437# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 438# Training
 439# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 440
 441def soft_erode(x):
 442    """Soft erosion of ``(B, 1, H, W)`` maps in [0, 1]: the minimum over each pixel and its four neighbours
 443    (Shit et al., 2021). Past the frame's edge counts as branch, so a trunk leaving the frame is not eaten
 444    from its cut end.
 445
 446    Args:
 447        x: ``(B, 1, H, W)`` tensor of maps in [0, 1].
 448
 449    Returns:
 450        The eroded maps, the same shape.
 451    """
 452    import torch
 453    import torch.nn.functional as F
 454
 455    return torch.min(-F.max_pool2d(-x, (3, 1), 1, (1, 0)), -F.max_pool2d(-x, (1, 3), 1, (0, 1)))
 456
 457
 458def soft_dilate(x):
 459    """Soft dilation of ``(B, 1, H, W)`` maps: the maximum over each pixel's 3x3 neighbourhood.
 460
 461    Args:
 462        x: ``(B, 1, H, W)`` tensor of maps in [0, 1].
 463
 464    Returns:
 465        The dilated maps, the same shape.
 466    """
 467    import torch.nn.functional as F
 468
 469    return F.max_pool2d(x, 3, 1, 1)
 470
 471
 472def soft_skeleton(x, iters: int = CL_ITERS):
 473    """A differentiable centre line of ``(B, 1, H, W)`` maps in [0, 1] (Shit et al., 2021).
 474
 475    The map is eroded ``iters`` times; at each step what an opening (erosion
 476    then dilation) removes is the part that thins out there, and it is added
 477    to the skeleton where not already counted. On a binary mask the result
 478    is a one- or two-pixel centre line; on probabilities it is soft, so the
 479    loss can push along it. A branch wider than ``iters`` erosions keeps no
 480    centre line (:data:`CL_ITERS`).
 481
 482    Args:
 483        x: ``(B, 1, H, W)`` tensor of maps in [0, 1].
 484        iters: Erosions.
 485
 486    Returns:
 487        The soft centre lines, the same shape.
 488    """
 489    import torch.nn.functional as F
 490
 491    skel = F.relu(x - soft_dilate(soft_erode(x)))
 492    for _ in range(iters):
 493        x = soft_erode(x)
 494        delta = F.relu(x - soft_dilate(soft_erode(x)))
 495        skel = skel + F.relu(delta - skel * delta)         # add only what is not yet on the skeleton
 496    return skel
 497
 498
 499def soft_cldice_loss(p, target, iters: int = CL_ITERS, smooth: float = 1.0):
 500    """``1 − clDice`` of soft masks, per photo (Shit et al., 2021): the soft version of :func:`cl_dice`.
 501
 502    Topology precision is the share of the prediction's soft centre line
 503    that lies in the target, topology sensitivity the share of the target's
 504    centre line that lies in the prediction; clDice is their harmonic mean.
 505    A leader that stops short or breaks loses sensitivity even when it costs
 506    few pixels; a side branch the target does not have loses precision.
 507
 508    Args:
 509        p: ``(B, H, W)`` probabilities.
 510        target: ``(B, H, W)`` masks in [0, 1].
 511        iters: Erosions of :func:`soft_skeleton`.
 512        smooth: Added to both sides of each ratio (as the Dice term's 1).
 513
 514    Returns:
 515        ``(B,)`` losses in [0, 1].
 516    """
 517    sp, st = soft_skeleton(p.unsqueeze(1), iters)[:, 0], soft_skeleton(target.unsqueeze(1), iters)[:, 0]
 518    prec = ((sp * target).sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth) / (sp.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth)
 519    sens = ((st * p).sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth) / (st.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth)
 520    return 1 - 2 * prec * sens / (prec + sens)
 521
 522
 523def seg_loss(logits, target, known=None, cldice: float = 0.0, iters: int = CL_ITERS):
 524    """Binary cross-entropy plus soft Dice loss (``1 − 2|P∩T| / (|P| + |T|)``, per photo, smoothed by 1),
 525    and, with ``cldice`` = α > 0, the centre-line loss: ``BCE + (1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice``.
 526
 527    Args:
 528        logits: ``(B, H, W)`` network outputs.
 529        target: ``(B, H, W)`` masks in [0, 1] (soft at resampled edges).
 530        known: Optional ``(B, H, W)`` or ``(H, W)`` weights in [0, 1]: where
 531            the masks say something (1) or nothing (0, the whole photo's side
 532            columns). Pixels of weight 0 count in neither term; None counts
 533            every pixel, exactly as before.
 534        cldice: Weight of :func:`soft_cldice_loss` (:data:`CLDICE_WEIGHT` when
 535            used); 0 returns exactly the loss of the named recipe.
 536        iters: The soft skeleton's erosions (:data:`CL_ITERS`).
 537
 538    Returns:
 539        The loss, a scalar tensor.
 540    """
 541    import torch
 542    import torch.nn.functional as F
 543
 544    p = torch.sigmoid(logits)
 545    if known is None:
 546        bce = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, target)
 547    else:
 548        known = known.expand_as(target)
 549        bce = ((F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, target, reduction="none") * known).sum()
 550               / known.sum().clamp_min(1.0))
 551        p, target = p * known, target * known
 552    inter = (p * target).sum(dim=(1, 2))
 553    dice = 1 - (2 * inter + 1) / (p.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + target.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + 1)
 554    if not cldice:
 555        return bce + dice.mean()                            # the named recipe, unchanged
 556    return bce + (1 - cldice) * dice.mean() + cldice * soft_cldice_loss(p, target, iters).mean()
 557
 558
 559def _loss_options(params: SegParams) -> dict:
 560    """The recipe's extra :func:`seg_loss` arguments: none for the named recipe, so its calls stay as they were."""
 561    return {"cldice": params.cldice, "iters": params.cl_iters} if params.cldice else {}
 562
 563
 564def augment_pair(x, m, generator, params: SegParams = SegParams(), flip_p: float = 0.5, known=None):
 565    """Random crop, rotation, mirror image and colour jitter, with the mask resampled alike.
 566
 567    The crop, rotation and mirror are one affine resampling per photo: a
 568    fraction ``f`` of each side (``f² ∈ [crop, 1]`` of the area) at a random
 569    position. The rotation is made in pixels, so it keeps angles in a
 570    non-square frame too (in a square one the arithmetic is unchanged).
 571
 572    Args:
 573        x: ``(B, C, H, W)`` floats in [0, 1] (C = 3, or 4 with the depth last,
 574            which is not jittered).
 575        m: ``(B, H, W)`` masks in [0, 1].
 576        generator: A ``torch.Generator`` on ``x``'s device.
 577        params: ``crop``, ``rotate`` and ``jitter``.
 578        flip_p: Chance of the mirror image.
 579        known: Optional ``(H, W)`` or ``(B, H, W)`` weights (:func:`seg_loss`),
 580            resampled with the mask; pixels brought in from past the edge are
 581            the edge's.
 582
 583    Returns:
 584        ``(images, masks)``: normalised images and masks in [0, 1], same
 585        shapes; with ``known``, ``(images, masks, known)``.
 586    """
 587    import torch
 588    import torch.nn.functional as F
 589
 590    b, dev = x.shape[0], x.device
 591    aspect = x.shape[-1] / x.shape[-2]                                       # width / height
 592
 593    def uniform(lo, hi):
 594        """``b`` random numbers between ``lo`` and ``hi``, one per image."""
 595        return lo + (hi - lo) * torch.rand(b, device=dev, generator=generator)
 596
 597    f = torch.sqrt(uniform(params.crop, 1.0))
 598    a = torch.deg2rad(uniform(-params.rotate, params.rotate))
 599    tx, ty = uniform(-1.0, 1.0) * (1 - f), uniform(-1.0, 1.0) * (1 - f)
 600    sx = torch.where(torch.rand(b, device=dev, generator=generator) < flip_p, -f, f)
 601    theta = torch.zeros(b, 2, 3, device=dev)
 602    cos, sin = torch.cos(a), torch.sin(a)
 603    # Rotation after the mirror and scale, in pixels: in the grid's [-1, 1] coordinates the off-diagonal
 604    # terms carry the frame's aspect ratio (1 for a square frame).
 605    theta[:, 0, 0], theta[:, 0, 1], theta[:, 0, 2] = cos * sx, -sin * f / aspect, tx
 606    theta[:, 1, 0], theta[:, 1, 1], theta[:, 1, 2] = sin * sx * aspect, cos * f, ty
 607    parts = [x, m.unsqueeze(1)]
 608    if known is not None:
 609        parts.append(known.expand(b, *m.shape[-2:]).unsqueeze(1).to(x.dtype))
 610    both = torch.cat(parts, dim=1)
 611    grid = F.affine_grid(theta, list(both.shape), align_corners=False)
 612    both = F.grid_sample(both, grid, mode="bilinear", padding_mode="border", align_corners=False)
 613    c = x.shape[1]
 614    x, m = both[:, :c], both[:, c].clamp(0, 1)
 615    if known is not None:
 616        known = both[:, c + 1].clamp(0, 1)
 617    j = params.jitter
 618    if j > 0:
 619        rgb, rest = x[:, :3], x[:, 3:]
 620        rgb = rgb * uniform(1 - j, 1 + j).view(b, 1, 1, 1)                     # brightness
 621        mean = rgb.mean(dim=(1, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
 622        rgb = (rgb - mean) * uniform(1 - j, 1 + j).view(b, 1, 1, 1) + mean      # contrast
 623        grey = (0.299 * rgb[:, 0] + 0.587 * rgb[:, 1] + 0.114 * rgb[:, 2]).unsqueeze(1)
 624        rgb = grey + (rgb - grey) * uniform(1 - j, 1 + j).view(b, 1, 1, 1)      # saturation
 625        x = torch.cat([rgb.clamp(0, 1), rest], dim=1)
 626    return (normalise(x), m) if known is None else (normalise(x), m, known)
 627
 628
 629def _float(x_uint8):
 630    return x_uint8.float().div_(255.0)
 631
 632
 633def predict_masks(model, x_uint8, batch: int = 16) -> np.ndarray:
 634    """Branch probabilities, each the average of the photo's and (flipped back) its mirror image's.
 635
 636    Args:
 637        model: The network.
 638        x_uint8: ``(N, C, S, S)`` uint8 tensor on the model's device.
 639        batch: Photos per forward pass.
 640
 641    Returns:
 642        ``(N, H, W)`` float32 probabilities.
 643    """
 644    import torch
 645
 646    model.eval()
 647    out = []
 648    with torch.inference_mode():
 649        for i in range(0, len(x_uint8), batch):
 650            x = normalise(_float(x_uint8[i:i + batch]))
 651            p = (torch.sigmoid(model(x)) + torch.sigmoid(model(x.flip(-1))).flip(-1)) / 2
 652            out.append(p.float().cpu().numpy())
 653    return np.concatenate(out) if out else np.zeros((0,) + tuple(x_uint8.shape[-2:]), np.float32)
 654
 655
 656def train_seg(model, x_uint8, m_uint8, epochs: int, params: SegParams, seed: int, val: tuple | None = None,
 657              on_epoch: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
 658    """Train ``model`` in place: AdamW with a cosine learning-rate decay over ``epochs``.
 659
 660    Args:
 661        model: The :class:`UNet`, on its device.
 662        x_uint8: ``(N, C, H, W)`` uint8 tensor of training photos on the device.
 663        m_uint8: ``(N, H, W)`` uint8 tensor of their masks (0–255).
 664        epochs: Epochs to train.
 665        params: The recipe.
 666        seed: Seed for the batch order and the augmentation.
 667        val: Optional ``(x_uint8, m_uint8)`` held out; its loss (on the
 668            mirror-averaged probabilities) is recorded after each epoch.
 669        on_epoch: Called with each epoch's record.
 670
 671    Returns:
 672        One record per epoch: ``{"epoch", "train_loss", "val_loss"}``.
 673    """
 674    import torch
 675
 676    dev = x_uint8.device
 677    torch.manual_seed(seed)
 678    km = known_map(params)                                  # None in the masks' own frame
 679    known = None if km is None else torch.from_numpy(km).to(dev)
 680    gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
 681    # The pretrained encoder is only adjusted (a small learning rate); the new decoder learns from scratch.
 682    enc, dec = model.groups()
 683    opt = torch.optim.AdamW([{"params": enc, "lr": params.lr_encoder}, {"params": dec, "lr": params.lr_decoder}],
 684                            weight_decay=params.weight_decay)
 685    n = len(x_uint8)
 686    steps = max(1, math.ceil(n / params.batch)) * max(1, epochs)
 687    # The learning rate falls along half a cosine, from its full value at the first step to 0 at the last.
 688    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(opt, lambda step: 0.5 * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * min(step, steps) / steps)))
 689    extra = _loss_options(params)                           # the centre-line term, if the recipe has one
 690    log = []
 691    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
 692        model.train()
 693        order = torch.randperm(n, device=dev, generator=gen)    # a new order of the photos every epoch
 694        total, count = 0.0, 0
 695        for i in range(0, n, params.batch):
 696            idx = order[i:i + params.batch]
 697            if len(idx) < 2:                                   # batch norm needs two photos
 698                continue
 699            # Each batch is augmented afresh (crop, rotation, mirror, colour), the masks moved with their photos.
 700            if known is None:
 701                x, m = augment_pair(_float(x_uint8[idx]), _float(m_uint8[idx]), gen, params)
 702                loss = seg_loss(model(x), m, **extra)
 703            else:
 704                x, m, k = augment_pair(_float(x_uint8[idx]), _float(m_uint8[idx]), gen, params, known=known)
 705                loss = seg_loss(model(x), m, k, **extra)
 706            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
 707            loss.backward()
 708            opt.step()
 709            sched.step()
 710            total, count = total + loss.item() * len(idx), count + len(idx)
 711        record = {"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": total / max(count, 1), "val_loss": None}
 712        if val is not None:
 713            # The held-out loss is on the prediction as it will be made (mirror image averaged in), so the
 714            # probabilities are turned back into logits for the same loss function.
 715            p = torch.as_tensor(predict_masks(model, val[0])).clamp(1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
 716            # The epochs are chosen by the recipe's own loss, centre-line term included. That term's soft
 717            # skeleton takes seconds per epoch on a CPU, so it is computed where the network runs; the named
 718            # recipe's loss stays on the CPU, exactly as before.
 719            where = dev if extra else "cpu"
 720            record["val_loss"] = float(seg_loss(torch.logit(p).to(where), _float(val[1]).to(where),
 721                                               None if known is None else known.to(where), **extra))
 722        log.append(record)
 723        if on_epoch:
 724            on_epoch(record)
 725    return log
 726
 727
 728def cross_validate_seg(images: np.ndarray, masks: np.ndarray, has_mask: np.ndarray, rows: np.ndarray,
 729                       fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]], params: SegParams = SegParams(), device: str | None = None,
 730                       pretrained: bool = True, progress: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> dict:
 731    """Train and predict every tree from the fold that holds its row out (see the module docstring).
 732
 733    Args:
 734        images: ``(n, H, W, C)`` uint8 summer photos at ``params.size`` (:func:`load_frames`).
 735        masks: ``(n, H, W)`` uint8 hand masks (0–255) in the same frame.
 736        has_mask: ``(n,)`` bool; trees without a hand mask are predicted but never trained on.
 737        rows: ``(n,)`` orchard rows.
 738        fold_rows: Each fold's held-out rows (``splits.json``).
 739        params: The recipe.
 740        device: ``"cuda"``, ``"cpu"``, or None for the GPU if there is one.
 741        pretrained: Start from the ImageNet weights (False: random, for tests).
 742        progress: Where progress lines go.
 743
 744    Returns:
 745        ``{"prob": (n, H, W) float32, "fold": (n,), "epochs": [...], "log": [...], "device": str}``.
 746    """
 747    import torch
 748
 749    device = device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
 750    torch.manual_seed(params.seed)                          # the decoder's first weights
 751    base = UNet(params.encoder, pretrained, channels=images.shape[3]).to(device)
 752    start = copy.deepcopy(base.state_dict())
 753    x_all = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(images.transpose(0, 3, 1, 2))).to(device)
 754    m_all = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(masks)).to(device)
 755    n = len(images)
 756    prob, fold = np.full((n,) + images.shape[1:3], np.nan, np.float32), np.full(n, -1)
 757    chosen, logs = [], []
 758
 759    def fresh():
 760        """The network reset to its starting weights (one copy reused, to save memory)."""
 761        base.load_state_dict(start)
 762        return base
 763
 764    def take(sel):
 765        """The photos and masks selected by the boolean ``sel``."""
 766        idx = torch.from_numpy(np.nonzero(sel)[0]).to(device)
 767        return x_all[idx], m_all[idx]
 768
 769    for i, held in enumerate(fold_rows):
 770        # This fold's rows are predicted; the network trains on the other rows' trees that have a hand mask.
 771        va = np.isin(rows, list(held))
 772        tr = ~va & has_mask
 773        if not va.any() or tr.sum() < 2:
 774            continue
 775        t0 = time.time()
 776        # The number of epochs is chosen inside the training rows: the next fold's rows are held out, and the
 777        # epoch with the lowest loss on them is kept. The fold's own rows play no part in the choice.
 778        inner = _inner_rows(i, fold_rows, set(rows[tr].tolist()), rows[has_mask])
 779        best = params.epochs
 780        if inner is not None:
 781            iv = tr & np.isin(rows, inner)
 782            it = tr & ~iv
 783            progress(f"Fold {i + 1}/{len(fold_rows)} (rows {sorted(map(int, held))}, {_n(va.sum(), 'tree')}): "
 784                     f"choosing the epochs on rows {sorted(map(int, inner))} ({_n(iv.sum(), 'tree')})...")
 785            log = train_seg(fresh(), *take(it), params.epochs, params, params.seed + 100 * i, val=take(iv),
 786                            on_epoch=lambda r: (progress(f"  epoch {r['epoch']:3d}: train {r['train_loss']:.3f}, "
 787                                                         f"held out {r['val_loss']:.3f}")
 788                                                if r["epoch"] % 5 == 0 or r["epoch"] == 1 else None))
 789            logs += [{"fold": i, "stage": "choose", **r} for r in log]
 790            best = int(min(log, key=lambda r: r["val_loss"])["epoch"])
 791            progress(f"  lowest held-out loss after {_n(best, 'epoch')}")
 792        else:
 793            progress(f"Fold {i + 1}/{len(fold_rows)}: no rows to hold out inside the training rows; "
 794                     f"training for {_n(best, 'epoch')}")
 795        # Then a fresh network trains on all the training rows for that many epochs and predicts the fold.
 796        log = train_seg(fresh(), *take(tr), best, params, params.seed + 100 * i + 50)
 797        logs += [{"fold": i, "stage": "final", **r} for r in log]
 798        prob[va] = predict_masks(base, take(va)[0])
 799        fold[va] = i
 800        chosen.append({"fold": i, "epochs": best, "inner_rows": inner, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)})
 801        progress(f"  trained on {_n(tr.sum(), 'tree')} for {_n(best, 'epoch')}; fold done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
 802    return {"prob": prob, "fold": fold, "epochs": chosen, "log": logs, "device": device}
 803

 805# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 806# Scoring
 807# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 808
 809def prob_frame(prob: np.ndarray, whole: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
 810    """Probabilities in the hand masks' 256x256 frame (float32), resized bilinearly.
 811
 812    Args:
 813        prob: ``(S, S)`` probabilities in the masks' frame, or, with ``whole``,
 814            ``(H, W)`` over the whole photo, whose centre columns
 815            (:func:`known_columns`) are the masks' frame.
 816        whole: ``prob`` covers the whole photo.
 817
 818    Returns:
 819        ``(256, 256)`` float32 probabilities.
 820    """
 821    from PIL import Image
 822
 823    from treeskel.io import MASK_SHAPE
 824
 825    p = np.asarray(prob, np.float32)
 826    if whole:
 827        a, b = known_columns(p.shape[1])
 828        p = np.ascontiguousarray(p[:, a:b])
 829    if p.shape != MASK_SHAPE:
 830        p = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(p).resize(MASK_SHAPE[::-1], Image.BILINEAR))
 831    return p
 832
 833
 834def to_mask_size(prob: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 0.5, whole: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
 835    """Probabilities to a 256x256 bool mask in the hand masks' frame (:func:`prob_frame`), thresholded.
 836
 837    Args:
 838        prob: As :func:`prob_frame`.
 839        threshold: Probability above which a pixel is branch.
 840        whole: ``prob`` covers the whole photo.
 841
 842    Returns:
 843        ``(256, 256)`` boolean mask.
 844    """
 845    return prob_frame(prob, whole) > threshold
 846
 847
 848def mask_scores(pred: np.ndarray, truth: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
 849    """IoU, Dice, precision and recall of a predicted mask against a hand mask (NaN where undefined).
 850
 851    Args:
 852        pred: Predicted boolean mask.
 853        truth: Hand boolean mask, the same shape.
 854
 855    Returns:
 856        ``{"iou", "dice", "precision", "recall"}``.
 857    """
 858    p, t = np.asarray(pred, bool), np.asarray(truth, bool)
 859    tp = float((p & t).sum())
 860    fp, fn = float((p & ~t).sum()), float((~p & t).sum())
 861
 862    def ratio(a, b):
 863        """``a / b``, or NaN when ``b`` is 0."""
 864        return a / b if b > 0 else float("nan")
 865
 866    return {"iou": ratio(tp, tp + fp + fn), "dice": ratio(2 * tp, 2 * tp + fp + fn),
 867            "precision": ratio(tp, tp + fp), "recall": ratio(tp, tp + fn)}
 868
 869
 870def mask_shape(mask: np.ndarray, params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams()) -> tuple[dict[str, float], dict | None]:
 871    """The shape measures of a 256x256 mask, measured as the hand masks are.
 872
 873    Args:
 874        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
 875        params: The shape measures' settings.
 876
 877    Returns:
 878        ``(measures, branches)``: :func:`treeskel.shape.shape_measures` (NaN
 879        throughout if no fork is found) and :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches`'s paths (or None).
 880    """
 881    br = mask_branches(np.asarray(mask, bool))
 882    if br is None:
 883        return dict.fromkeys(MEASURES, float("nan")), None
 884    return shape_measures(br["trunk"], br["left"], br["right"], br["fork_radius"], params, MASK_ZOOM), br
 885
 886
 887JOIN_GAP = 19.3
 888"""Largest gap (mask px, nearest pixel centre to nearest pixel centre) that :func:`join_pieces` bridges:
 889about a trunk's width. It is twice the development hand masks' median trunk radius at the fork (9.67
 890mask px as :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches` measures it, the distance from the centre line to the
 891nearest background pixel; 448 trees), so up to about 18 background pixels, 36 px of the photo. Fixed
 892from that geometry before any joined mask was scored (session 12); never tuned on the winter traces."""
 893
 894
 895def join_pieces(mask: np.ndarray, gap: float = JOIN_GAP) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
 896    """Join the pieces of a broken predicted mask to its largest piece across gaps of at most ``gap``.
 897
 898    :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches` keeps only the largest piece, so a
 899    leader cut from the trunk by a few pixels of leaves is lost, and with it
 900    the fork. Here, starting from the largest piece, the nearest other piece
 901    is joined if its nearest pixel is within ``gap`` of the joined mask, and
 902    so on until none is (a piece may come within reach through one joined
 903    before it). The join is a straight band between the two pieces' nearest
 904    centre-line (skeleton) points, as wide as the narrower of the two near
 905    there (the widest point of each centre line within ``gap`` of the join),
 906    so the centre lines run on through it. Pixels are only added, and a mask
 907    in one piece is returned unchanged.
 908
 909    Args:
 910        mask: ``(H, W)`` bool predicted mask.
 911        gap: Largest gap bridged (px, nearest pixel centre to nearest pixel
 912            centre); 0 joins nothing.
 913
 914    Returns:
 915        ``(joined mask, number of pieces joined)``.
 916    """
 917    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
 918    from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
 919
 920    out = np.asarray(mask, bool).copy()
 921    filled = ndi.binary_fill_holes(out)
 922    lab, n = ndi.label(filled, np.ones((3, 3)))
 923    if n < 2 or gap <= 0:
 924        return out, 0
 925    sizes = ndi.sum(filled, lab, range(1, n + 1))
 926    first = int(np.argmax(sizes)) + 1
 927    main = lab == first
 928    rest = [k for k in range(1, n + 1) if k != first]
 929    half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(filled)        # at a centre-line point: the piece's half-width
 930    joined = 0
 931    while rest:
 932        to_main = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~main)         # distance to the nearest pixel of the joined mask
 933        near = {k: float(to_main[lab == k].min()) for k in rest}
 934        k = min(near, key=near.get)
 935        if near[k] > gap:
 936            break
 937        piece = lab == k
 938        # The two nearest centre-line points: one on the piece, one on the joined mask.
 939        sk_main, sk_piece = skeletonize(main), skeletonize(piece)
 940        d, (iy, ix) = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~sk_main, return_indices=True)
 941        ys, xs = np.nonzero(sk_piece)
 942        j = int(np.argmin(d[ys, xs]))
 943        a, b = (int(ys[j]), int(xs[j])), (int(iy[ys[j], xs[j]]), int(ix[ys[j], xs[j]]))
 944        width = min(_widest_near(half_width, sk_piece, a, gap), _widest_near(half_width, sk_main, b, gap))
 945        band = _band(out.shape, a, b, width)
 946        out |= band
 947        main |= piece | band
 948        rest.remove(k)
 949        joined += 1
 950    return out, joined
 951
 952
 953def _band(shape: tuple[int, int], a: tuple[int, int], b: tuple[int, int], width: float) -> np.ndarray:
 954    """The pixels within ``width`` (at least 1) of the straight line from ``a`` to ``b``: a join's band."""
 955    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
 956    from skimage.draw import line as draw_line
 957
 958    line = np.zeros(shape, bool)
 959    line[draw_line(*a, *b)] = True
 960    return ndi.distance_transform_edt(~line) < max(1.0, width)
 961
 962
 963def _widest_near(half_width: np.ndarray, skeleton: np.ndarray, point: tuple[int, int], reach: float) -> float:
 964    """The largest half-width on a centre line within ``reach`` of ``point``: the branch's own half-width
 965    near a join, not the smaller one where the centre line ends short of a cut face."""
 966    ys, xs = np.nonzero(skeleton)
 967    near = np.hypot(ys - point[0], xs - point[1]) <= max(reach, 1.0)
 968    return float(half_width[ys[near], xs[near]].max())
 969
 970
 971GROW_LOWS = (0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05)
 972"""The lower thresholds :func:`choose_low` tries for :func:`grow_mask`, fixed before any run (session 12);
 9730.5 grows nothing."""
 974
 975
 976def grow_mask(prob: np.ndarray, low: float, seed: np.ndarray | None = None, high: float = 0.5) -> np.ndarray:
 977    """Hysteresis thresholding: the confident mask plus every less sure pixel connected to it.
 978
 979    Where leaves hide a leader, the U-Net's probability often fades below the
 980    threshold before the leader ends, so the mask stops short or breaks. Here
 981    pixels above ``low`` are kept wherever they connect (8-connected, through
 982    other such pixels) to the confident mask; faint patches that touch no
 983    confident pixel stay out. It uses only the network's own output.
 984
 985    Args:
 986        prob: ``(H, W)`` probabilities.
 987        low: Lower threshold; ``low >= high`` grows nothing.
 988        seed: The confident mask (default ``prob > high``); pass the saved
 989            mask so that it is kept exactly.
 990        high: The threshold the mask was made with.
 991
 992    Returns:
 993        ``(H, W)`` bool: ``seed`` and the grown pixels.
 994    """
 995    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
 996
 997    p = np.asarray(prob, np.float32)
 998    seed = p > high if seed is None else np.asarray(seed, bool)
 999    candidates = seed | (p > low)
1000    lab, n = ndi.label(candidates, np.ones((3, 3)))
1001    keep = np.zeros(n + 1, bool)
1002    keep[np.unique(lab[seed])] = True
1003    keep[0] = False
1004    return keep[lab]
1005
1006
1007def cl_dice(pred: np.ndarray, truth: np.ndarray) -> float:
1008    """Centre-line Dice (Shit et al., 2021): how well two masks' centre lines lie in each other.
1009
1010    The harmonic mean of the fraction of the prediction's centre line inside
1011    the truth (topology precision) and of the truth's centre line inside the
1012    prediction (topology sensitivity). A leader that stops short or breaks
1013    loses sensitivity; growth into leaves beside the branch loses precision.
1014    Unlike the pixel Dice, it is not dominated by the wide trunk. NaN if
1015    either mask is empty.
1016
1017    Args:
1018        pred: Predicted boolean mask.
1019        truth: Hand boolean mask, the same shape.
1020
1021    Returns:
1022        The centre-line Dice in [0, 1], or NaN.
1023    """
1024    from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
1025
1026    p, t = np.asarray(pred, bool), np.asarray(truth, bool)
1027    sp, st = skeletonize(p), skeletonize(t)
1028    if not sp.any() or not st.any():
1029        return float("nan")
1030    prec, sens = (sp & t).sum() / sp.sum(), (st & p).sum() / st.sum()
1031    return float(2 * prec * sens / (prec + sens)) if prec + sens > 0 else 0.0
1032
1033
1034def choose_low(probs: dict[str, np.ndarray], seeds: dict[str, np.ndarray], hands: dict[str, np.ndarray],
1035               lows: Sequence[float] = GROW_LOWS, gap: float = JOIN_GAP,
1036               progress: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> tuple[float, dict[str, float]]:
1037    """The lower threshold of :func:`grow_mask` whose masks, grown and joined, best match the hand masks'
1038    centre lines (mean :func:`cl_dice` over the trees with a hand mask). The winter traces play no part.
1039
1040    Args:
1041        probs: ``{tree: (256, 256) probabilities}`` in the masks' frame, each from the fold that held it out.
1042        seeds: ``{tree: the saved mask}``.
1043        hands: ``{tree: its (lined-up) hand mask}``.
1044        lows: The thresholds tried; on a tie the higher (less growth) wins.
1045        gap: The joining gap applied after growing, as in the scored masks.
1046        progress: Prints a progress line.
1047
1048    Returns:
1049        ``(chosen low, {str(low): mean clDice})``.
1050    """
1051    trees = [t for t in probs if t in hands]
1052    table = {}
1053    for low in lows:
1054        vals = [cl_dice(join_pieces(grow_mask(probs[t], low, seeds[t]), gap)[0], hands[t]) for t in trees]
1055        table[f"{low:g}"] = float(np.nanmean(vals))
1056        progress(f"  lower threshold {low:<4g}: mean clDice {table[f'{low:g}']:.4f} ({len(trees)} trees)")
1057    best = max(lows, key=lambda v: (round(table[f"{v:g}"], 6), v))
1058    return float(best), table
1059
1060
1061def save_probabilities(path: Path, ids: Sequence[str], probs: np.ndarray) -> None:
1062    """Probability maps of many trees in the masks' frame, as uint8 (``round(255 p)``) in one ``.npz``.
1063
1064    Args:
1065        path: The ``.npz`` file.
1066        ids: Tree ids, one per map.
1067        probs: ``(n, 256, 256)`` probabilities in [0, 1].
1068    """
1069    q = np.round(np.clip(np.asarray(probs, np.float32), 0, 1) * 255).astype(np.uint8)
1070    np.savez_compressed(path, ids=np.array(ids), prob=q)
1071
1072
1073def load_probabilities(path: Path) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
1074    """Inverse of :func:`save_probabilities`: ``{tree: (256, 256) float32 in [0, 1]}``.
1075
1076    Args:
1077        path: A file from :func:`save_probabilities`.
1078
1079    Returns:
1080        The maps per tree id.
1081    """
1082    with np.load(path) as z:
1083        return {str(t): z["prob"][i].astype(np.float32) / 255 for i, t in enumerate(z["ids"])}
1084
1085
1086CONTINUE_CONE = 25.0
1087"""Largest angle (degrees) between a short leader's direction at its tip and a piece that
1088:func:`continue_leaders` joins to it: the development hand masks' leaders turn by at most 24.8 degrees
1089between the two halves of the fitted stretch in 95% of cases (896 leaders), so a piece further off that
1090line is more likely another branch than the same leader. Fixed before any continued mask was scored
1091(session 12); never tuned on the winter traces."""
1092
1093
1094def _tip_direction(path: np.ndarray, length: float) -> np.ndarray:
1095    """Unit ``(row, col)`` direction of a leader at its tip: a line through its last ``length`` px, pointing out."""
1096    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1097    from treeskel.shape import line_direction, to_xy
1098
1099    p = np.asarray(path, float)
1100    s = arc_length(p)
1101    end = p[s >= s[-1] - length]
1102    if len(end) < 2:
1103        end = p[-2:]
1104    d = line_direction(to_xy(end))                          # (x, y), y up
1105    d = np.array([-d[1], d[0]])                            # (row, col)
1106    return d if np.dot(d, end[-1] - end[0]) >= 0 else -d
1107
1108
1109def continue_leaders(mask: np.ndarray, cone: float = CONTINUE_CONE, params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams(),
1110                     rounds: int = 5) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
1111    """Join pieces lying on a short leader's way on, then keep only the trunk and the two leaders.
1112
1113    The student's idea (session 12): where leaves hide a leader, the mask
1114    often stops, and a piece of the same leader lies further along its line,
1115    too far for :func:`join_pieces`. Here, for each leader shorter than the
1116    stretch the angles are fitted over (``params.reach`` units at
1117    :data:`treeskel.shape.MASK_ZOOM`), the pieces of the mask not joined to
1118    the tree are searched: one is joined if some pixel of it lies within the
1119    part of the stretch still missing (``reach`` minus the leader's length)
1120    of the tip and within ``cone`` degrees of the leader's direction at its
1121    tip (a line through its last ``params.trunk_reach`` units, the length of
1122    the trunk's axis), and it has at least ``params.min_points`` px of
1123    centre line. The nearest such piece is joined by a band from the tip to
1124    its nearest centre-line point, as :func:`join_pieces` joins; the leaders
1125    are found again and the search repeats (a chain of pieces), up to
1126    ``rounds`` times. Finally the mask is cut down to the trunk and the two
1127    leaders (:func:`prune_to_branches`).
1128
1129    Args:
1130        mask: ``(256, 256)`` bool mask, already joined (:func:`join_pieces`).
1131        cone: :data:`CONTINUE_CONE`.
1132        params: The shape measures' stretch.
1133        rounds: Most joins per leader search.
1134
1135    Returns:
1136        ``(the trunk and leaders, pieces joined)``; a mask with no fork is returned unchanged.
1137    """
1138    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
1139    from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
1140
1141    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1142    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px
1143
1144    out = np.asarray(mask, bool).copy()
1145    unit = unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1146    reach, tip_len = params.reach * unit, params.trunk_reach * unit
1147    joined = 0
1148    br = mask_branches(out)
1149    if br is None:
1150        return out, 0
1151    for _ in range(rounds):
1152        # The mask's pieces; the tree is the piece holding the trunk's top.
1153        filled = ndi.binary_fill_holes(out)
1154        lab, n = ndi.label(filled, np.ones((3, 3)))
1155        tree = lab[tuple(br["trunk"][-1])]
1156        half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(filled)
1157        best = None                                         # (distance, side, piece label)
1158        for side in ("left", "right"):
1159            path = br[side]
1160            length = float(arc_length(path)[-1]) if len(path) > 1 else 0.0
1161            if length >= reach or len(path) < 2:
1162                continue
1163            tip, d = np.asarray(path[-1], float), _tip_direction(path, tip_len)
1164            # A candidate piece has a pixel within the missing stretch of the tip and inside the cone
1165            # around the leader's direction (cosine test: v . d >= |v| cos(cone)).
1166            for k in range(1, n + 1):
1167                if k == tree:
1168                    continue
1169                ys, xs = np.nonzero(lab == k)
1170                v = np.stack([ys, xs], 1) - tip
1171                dist = np.hypot(v[:, 0], v[:, 1])
1172                ok = (dist <= reach - length) & (v @ d >= np.cos(np.radians(cone)) * dist)
1173                if not ok.any() or skeletonize(lab == k).sum() < params.min_points:
1174                    continue
1175                if best is None or dist[ok].min() < best[0]:
1176                    best = (float(dist[ok].min()), side, k)
1177        if best is None:
1178            break
1179        # Join the nearest candidate: a band from the leader's tip to the piece's nearest centre-line point,
1180        # as wide as the narrower of the two ends (as join_pieces joins).
1181        _, side, k = best
1182        piece = lab == k
1183        sk_piece = skeletonize(piece)
1184        ys, xs = np.nonzero(sk_piece)
1185        tip = tuple(int(v) for v in br[side][-1])
1186        j = int(np.argmin(np.hypot(ys - tip[0], xs - tip[1])))
1187        b = (int(ys[j]), int(xs[j]))
1188        tree_line = np.zeros_like(out)
1189        tree_line[tuple(np.asarray(br[side]).T)] = True
1190        width = min(_widest_near(half_width, sk_piece, b, JOIN_GAP), _widest_near(half_width, tree_line, tip, JOIN_GAP))
1191        out |= _band(out.shape, tip, b, width)
1192        joined += 1
1193        found = mask_branches(out)                          # the leaders again, for the next round
1194        if found is None:                                   # cannot happen when joining to the tree; be safe
1195            break
1196        br = found
1197    return prune_to_branches(out, br), joined
1198
1199
1200def prune_to_branches(mask: np.ndarray, br: dict) -> np.ndarray:
1201    """The mask cut down to the trunk and the two leaders: its pixels within each path point's own half-width
1202    (the distance to the mask's edge there) of the paths :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches` found.
1203
1204    Args:
1205        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
1206        br: Its branches, from :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches`.
1207
1208    Returns:
1209        The pruned boolean mask.
1210    """
1211    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
1212
1213    filled = ndi.binary_fill_holes(np.asarray(mask, bool))
1214    half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(filled)
1215    pts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(br[p]).reshape(-1, 2) for p in ("trunk", "left", "right")])
1216    seeds = np.zeros(filled.shape, bool)
1217    seeds[pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1]] = True
1218    dist, (iy, ix) = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~seeds, return_indices=True)
1219    return filled & (dist < half_width[iy, ix])
1220
1221
1222COMPLETE_FRACTIONS = tuple(round(0.40 + 0.05 * i, 2) for i in range(12))
1223"""Where :func:`completion_samples` cuts complete leaders (fractions of the fitted stretch, 0.40-0.95): the
1224lengths short predicted leaders stop at (the re-run's joined masks: median 0.75 of the stretch, quartiles
12250.54-0.89; the named run's: 0.69, 0.42-0.88)."""
1226
1227
1228def _outward(path: np.ndarray, side: str, params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams()) -> tuple[float, float]:
1229    """A leader's line from the vertical, positive outwards, and its bend (as :func:`treeskel.shape.shape_measures`
1230    measures them in a mask), or NaN where the path is too short."""
1231    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, halves, leader_part, line_direction, tilt, to_xy, unit_px, wrap
1232
1233    part = leader_part(path, unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM), params)
1234    if len(part) < params.min_points:
1235        return float("nan"), float("nan")
1236    t = tilt(line_direction(to_xy(part)))
1237    low, up = halves(part)
1238    bend = float("nan")
1239    if min(len(low), len(up)) >= params.min_points:
1240        turn = wrap(tilt(line_direction(to_xy(up))) - tilt(line_direction(to_xy(low))))
1241        bend = turn if side == "right" else -turn
1242    return (t if side == "right" else -t), bend
1243
1244
1245def completion_samples(masks: dict[str, np.ndarray], params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams(),
1246                       fractions: Sequence[float] = COMPLETE_FRACTIONS) -> np.ndarray:
1247    """Complete leaders cut short on purpose: ``(n, 4)`` rows of ``(missing fraction g, outward line of the
1248    cut leader, its bend, outward line of the whole)``, for :func:`fit_completion`.
1249
1250    Every leader of ``masks`` that spans the whole fitted stretch is cut at each of ``fractions`` of it.
1251
1252    Args:
1253        masks: 256x256 boolean masks per tree id.
1254        params: The shape measures' settings.
1255        fractions: The fractions of the stretch cut off.
1256
1257    Returns:
1258        The samples.
1259    """
1260    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1261    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px
1262
1263    reach = params.reach * unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1264    rows = []
1265    for m in masks.values():
1266        _, br = mask_shape(m, params)
1267        if br is None:
1268            continue
1269        for side in ("left", "right"):
1270            s = arc_length(br[side]) if len(br[side]) > 1 else np.zeros(1)
1271            if s[-1] < reach:
1272                continue
1273            whole, _ = _outward(br[side], side, params)
1274            for f in fractions:
1275                cut, bend = _outward(br[side][s <= f * reach], side, params)
1276                if np.isfinite(cut) and np.isfinite(whole):
1277                    rows.append((1 - f, cut, bend, whole))
1278    return np.array(rows, float).reshape(-1, 4)
1279
1280
1281def fit_completion(samples: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
1282    """Least squares for the change of a leader's line over its missing part:
1283    ``whole − cut = a·g + c·g·bend`` (``g`` the missing fraction; a missing bend counts as 0).
1284
1285    Args:
1286        samples: From :func:`completion_samples`.
1287
1288    Returns:
1289        ``(a, c)``: the change (degrees) per unit of missing fraction, and per unit of missing fraction
1290        and bend.
1291    """
1292    g, cut, bend, whole = samples.T
1293    x = np.stack([g, g * np.nan_to_num(bend)], 1)
1294    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(x, whole - cut, rcond=None)
1295    return coef
1296
1297
1298def complete_measures(mask: np.ndarray, coef: Sequence[float], params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams()
1299                      ) -> tuple[dict[str, float], int]:
1300    """:func:`mask_shape` with each short leader's line predicted over the whole fitted stretch.
1301
1302    A leader shorter than the stretch has its line from the vertical moved
1303    by :func:`fit_completion`'s model (``a·g + c·g·bend``, outwards); the
1304    measures built on the leader lines (the V opening, the angles from the
1305    trunk, the V's lean, the tilts) follow. The bends stay as measured.
1306
1307    Args:
1308        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
1309        coef: ``(a, c)`` from :func:`fit_completion`.
1310        params: The shape measures' settings.
1311
1312    Returns:
1313        ``(measures, leaders completed)``.
1314    """
1315    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1316    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px, wrap
1317
1318    m, br = mask_shape(mask, params)
1319    if br is None:
1320        return m, 0
1321    reach = params.reach * unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1322    a, c = coef
1323    tilts, done = {}, 0
1324    for side in ("left", "right"):
1325        tilts[side] = m[f"{side}_tilt"]
1326        length = float(arc_length(br[side])[-1]) if len(br[side]) > 1 else 0.0
1327        if length >= reach or not np.isfinite(tilts[side]):
1328            continue
1329        g = 1 - length / reach
1330        _, bend = _outward(br[side], side, params)
1331        shift = a * g + c * g * (0.0 if not np.isfinite(bend) else bend)
1332        tilts[side] += shift if side == "right" else -shift
1333        done += 1
1334    if not done:
1335        return m, 0
1336    out = dict(m)
1337    out["left_tilt"], out["right_tilt"] = tilts["left"], tilts["right"]
1338    trunk = m["trunk_tilt"]
1339    if np.isfinite(tilts["left"]) and np.isfinite(tilts["right"]):
1340        out["v_opening"] = wrap(tilts["right"] - tilts["left"])
1341        out["lean_v"] = (tilts["left"] + tilts["right"]) / 2
1342        if np.isfinite(trunk):
1343            out["lean"] = wrap(out["lean_v"] - trunk)
1344    if np.isfinite(trunk):
1345        out["left_angle"] = wrap(trunk - tilts["left"]) if np.isfinite(tilts["left"]) else float("nan")
1346        out["right_angle"] = wrap(tilts["right"] - trunk) if np.isfinite(tilts["right"]) else float("nan")
1347    return out, done
1348
1349
1350def draw_completion(mask: np.ndarray, coef: Sequence[float], params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams()
1351                    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
1352    """The mask with each short leader drawn on over the missing part of the stretch, as :func:`complete_measures`
1353    predicts it: from the tip, along the leader's predicted line, as wide as the leader near its tip.
1354
1355    For showing the prediction (a leader that goes on through the leaves, not a stub); the scores come
1356    from :func:`complete_measures`.
1357
1358    Args:
1359        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
1360        coef: ``(a, c)`` from :func:`fit_completion`.
1361        params: The shape measures' settings.
1362
1363    Returns:
1364        ``(mask with the continuations, the continuations alone)``.
1365    """
1366    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
1367
1368    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1369    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px
1370
1371    out = np.asarray(mask, bool).copy()
1372    added = np.zeros_like(out)
1373    m, br = mask_shape(out, params)
1374    if br is None:
1375        return out, added
1376    reach = params.reach * unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1377    a, c = coef
1378    half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(ndi.binary_fill_holes(out))
1379    h, w = out.shape
1380    for side in ("left", "right"):
1381        path = np.asarray(br[side])
1382        length = float(arc_length(path)[-1]) if len(path) > 1 else 0.0
1383        if length >= reach or not np.isfinite(m[f"{side}_tilt"]):
1384            continue
1385        g = 1 - length / reach
1386        line, bend = _outward(path, side, params)
1387        whole = line + a * g + c * g * (0.0 if not np.isfinite(bend) else bend)
1388        angle = np.radians(whole if side == "right" else -whole)
1389        d = np.array([-np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)])     # (row, col), upwards
1390        tip = path[-1].astype(float)
1391        steps = np.arange(0.0, reach - length, 0.5)
1392        pts = tip + steps[:, None] * d
1393        inside = (pts[:, 0] >= 0) & (pts[:, 0] <= h - 1) & (pts[:, 1] >= 0) & (pts[:, 1] <= w - 1)
1394        if not inside.any():
1395            continue
1396        end = tuple(int(round(v)) for v in pts[np.nonzero(inside)[0][-1]])
1397        leader = np.zeros_like(out)
1398        leader[path[:, 0], path[:, 1]] = True
1399        width = _widest_near(half_width, leader, tuple(int(v) for v in tip), JOIN_GAP)
1400        added |= _band(out.shape, tuple(int(v) for v in tip), end, width) & ~out
1401    return out | added, added
1402
1403
1404def fill_failures(pred: np.ndarray, mean: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
1405    """Predictions with each tree whose mask gave no shape at all replaced by the mean shape.
1406
1407    A tree whose predicted mask has a fork but, say, no trunk axis keeps NaN on
1408    the trunk measures, as the winter trace and the hand mask of such a tree do.
1409
1410    Args:
1411        pred: ``(n, measures)`` predictions, NaN where a mask gave none.
1412        mean: ``(n, measures)``: each tree's fold's mean shape.
1413
1414    Returns:
1415        The filled ``(n, measures)`` predictions.
1416    """
1417    out = pred.copy()
1418    failed = ~np.isfinite(pred).any(axis=1)
1419    out[failed] = mean[failed]
1420    return out
1421
1422
1423def compare_with(seg: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]], other: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]],
1424                 names: Sequence[str] = MEASURES) -> dict:
1425    """The segmentation against another model, tree by tree, on the trees both predict.
1426
1427    Args:
1428        seg: The segmentation's ``{(tree, measure): (winter, prediction)}`` (:func:`read_predictions`).
1429        other: The other model's, in the same form.
1430        names: The measures compared.
1431
1432    Returns:
1433        ``{measure: {"n", "closer", "wilcoxon_p", "mae_seg", "mae_other"}}``: the fraction of trees the
1434        segmentation predicts more closely, and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the paired absolute errors.
1435    """
1436    from scipy import stats
1437
1438    out = {}
1439    for k in names:
1440        keys = [key for key in seg if key[1] == k and key in other]
1441        if len(keys) < 3:
1442            continue
1443        e_s = np.array([abs(seg[key][1] - seg[key][0]) for key in keys])
1444        e_o = np.array([abs(other[key][1] - other[key][0]) for key in keys])
1445        diff = e_o - e_s
1446        out[k] = {"n": len(keys), "closer": float(np.mean(diff > 0)),
1447                  "wilcoxon_p": float(stats.wilcoxon(diff).pvalue) if np.any(diff != 0) else 1.0,
1448                  "mae_seg": float(e_s.mean()), "mae_other": float(e_o.mean())}
1449    return out
1450
1451
1452def read_predictions(path: Path, column: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]]:
1453    """``{(tree, measure): (winter, prediction)}`` from a ``predictions.csv`` (this module's or
1454    :mod:`treeskel.shape_cnn`'s), where both are known.
1455
1456    Args:
1457        path: A ``predictions.csv``.
1458        column: The prediction's column (e.g. ``"segmentation"``).
1459
1460    Returns:
1461        The pairs.
1462    """
1463    got = {}
1464    with open(path, newline="") as f:
1465        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
1466            if r.get("winter") and r.get(column):
1467                got[(r["tree"], r["measure"])] = (float(r["winter"]), float(r[column]))
1468    return got
1469
