def soft_erode(x): 
442def soft_erode(x):
443    """Soft erosion of ``(B, 1, H, W)`` maps in [0, 1]: the minimum over each pixel and its four neighbours
444    (Shit et al., 2021). Past the frame's edge counts as branch, so a trunk leaving the frame is not eaten
445    from its cut end.
446
447    Args:
448        x: ``(B, 1, H, W)`` tensor of maps in [0, 1].
449
450    Returns:
451        The eroded maps, the same shape.
452    """
453    import torch
454    import torch.nn.functional as F
455
456    return torch.min(-F.max_pool2d(-x, (3, 1), 1, (1, 0)), -F.max_pool2d(-x, (1, 3), 1, (0, 1)))

Soft erosion of (B, 1, H, W) maps in [0, 1]: the minimum over each pixel and its four neighbours (Shit et al., 2021). Past the frame's edge counts as branch, so a trunk leaving the frame is not eaten from its cut end.

Arguments:
  • x: (B, 1, H, W) tensor of maps in [0, 1].
Returns:

The eroded maps, the same shape.

def soft_dilate(x): 
459def soft_dilate(x):
460    """Soft dilation of ``(B, 1, H, W)`` maps: the maximum over each pixel's 3x3 neighbourhood.
461
462    Args:
463        x: ``(B, 1, H, W)`` tensor of maps in [0, 1].
464
465    Returns:
466        The dilated maps, the same shape.
467    """
468    import torch.nn.functional as F
469
470    return F.max_pool2d(x, 3, 1, 1)

Soft dilation of (B, 1, H, W) maps: the maximum over each pixel's 3x3 neighbourhood.

Arguments:
  • x: (B, 1, H, W) tensor of maps in [0, 1].
Returns:

The dilated maps, the same shape.

def soft_skeleton(x, iters: int = 25): 
473def soft_skeleton(x, iters: int = CL_ITERS):
474    """A differentiable centre line of ``(B, 1, H, W)`` maps in [0, 1] (Shit et al., 2021).
475
476    The map is eroded ``iters`` times; at each step what an opening (erosion
477    then dilation) removes is the part that thins out there, and it is added
478    to the skeleton where not already counted. On a binary mask the result
479    is a one- or two-pixel centre line; on probabilities it is soft, so the
480    loss can push along it. A branch wider than ``iters`` erosions keeps no
481    centre line (:data:`CL_ITERS`).
482
483    Args:
484        x: ``(B, 1, H, W)`` tensor of maps in [0, 1].
485        iters: Erosions.
486
487    Returns:
488        The soft centre lines, the same shape.
489    """
490    import torch.nn.functional as F
491
492    skel = F.relu(x - soft_dilate(soft_erode(x)))
493    for _ in range(iters):
494        x = soft_erode(x)
495        delta = F.relu(x - soft_dilate(soft_erode(x)))
496        skel = skel + F.relu(delta - skel * delta)         # add only what is not yet on the skeleton
497    return skel

A differentiable centre line of (B, 1, H, W) maps in [0, 1] (Shit et al., 2021).

The map is eroded iters times; at each step what an opening (erosion then dilation) removes is the part that thins out there, and it is added to the skeleton where not already counted. On a binary mask the result is a one- or two-pixel centre line; on probabilities it is soft, so the loss can push along it. A branch wider than iters erosions keeps no centre line (CL_ITERS).

Arguments:
  • x: (B, 1, H, W) tensor of maps in [0, 1].
  • iters: Erosions.
Returns:

The soft centre lines, the same shape.

def soft_cldice_loss(p, target, iters: int = 25, smooth: float = 1.0): 
500def soft_cldice_loss(p, target, iters: int = CL_ITERS, smooth: float = 1.0):
501    """``1 − clDice`` of soft masks, per photo (Shit et al., 2021): the soft version of :func:`cl_dice`.
502
503    Topology precision is the share of the prediction's soft centre line
504    that lies in the target, topology sensitivity the share of the target's
505    centre line that lies in the prediction; clDice is their harmonic mean.
506    A leader that stops short or breaks loses sensitivity even when it costs
507    few pixels; a side branch the target does not have loses precision.
508
509    Args:
510        p: ``(B, H, W)`` probabilities.
511        target: ``(B, H, W)`` masks in [0, 1].
512        iters: Erosions of :func:`soft_skeleton`.
513        smooth: Added to both sides of each ratio (as the Dice term's 1).
514
515    Returns:
516        ``(B,)`` losses in [0, 1].
517    """
518    sp, st = soft_skeleton(p.unsqueeze(1), iters)[:, 0], soft_skeleton(target.unsqueeze(1), iters)[:, 0]
519    prec = ((sp * target).sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth) / (sp.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth)
520    sens = ((st * p).sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth) / (st.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + smooth)
521    return 1 - 2 * prec * sens / (prec + sens)

1 − clDice of soft masks, per photo (Shit et al., 2021): the soft version of cl_dice().

Topology precision is the share of the prediction's soft centre line that lies in the target, topology sensitivity the share of the target's centre line that lies in the prediction; clDice is their harmonic mean. A leader that stops short or breaks loses sensitivity even when it costs few pixels; a side branch the target does not have loses precision.

Arguments:
  • p: (B, H, W) probabilities.
  • target: (B, H, W) masks in [0, 1].
  • iters: Erosions of soft_skeleton().
  • smooth: Added to both sides of each ratio (as the Dice term's 1).
Returns:

(B,) losses in [0, 1].

def seg_loss(logits, target, known=None, cldice: float = 0.0, iters: int = 25): 
524def seg_loss(logits, target, known=None, cldice: float = 0.0, iters: int = CL_ITERS):
525    """Binary cross-entropy plus soft Dice loss (``1 − 2|P∩T| / (|P| + |T|)``, per photo, smoothed by 1),
526    and, with ``cldice`` = α > 0, the centre-line loss: ``BCE + (1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice``.
527
528    Args:
529        logits: ``(B, H, W)`` network outputs.
530        target: ``(B, H, W)`` masks in [0, 1] (soft at resampled edges).
531        known: Optional ``(B, H, W)`` or ``(H, W)`` weights in [0, 1]: where
532            the masks say something (1) or nothing (0, the whole photo's side
533            columns). Pixels of weight 0 count in neither term; None counts
534            every pixel, exactly as before.
535        cldice: Weight of :func:`soft_cldice_loss` (:data:`CLDICE_WEIGHT` when
536            used); 0 returns exactly the loss of the named recipe.
537        iters: The soft skeleton's erosions (:data:`CL_ITERS`).
538
539    Returns:
540        The loss, a scalar tensor.
541    """
542    import torch
543    import torch.nn.functional as F
544
545    p = torch.sigmoid(logits)
546    if known is None:
547        bce = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, target)
548    else:
549        known = known.expand_as(target)
550        bce = ((F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, target, reduction="none") * known).sum()
551               / known.sum().clamp_min(1.0))
552        p, target = p * known, target * known
553    inter = (p * target).sum(dim=(1, 2))
554    dice = 1 - (2 * inter + 1) / (p.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + target.sum(dim=(1, 2)) + 1)
555    if not cldice:
556        return bce + dice.mean()                            # the named recipe, unchanged
557    return bce + (1 - cldice) * dice.mean() + cldice * soft_cldice_loss(p, target, iters).mean()

Binary cross-entropy plus soft Dice loss (1 − 2|P∩T| / (|P| + |T|), per photo, smoothed by 1), and, with cldice = α > 0, the centre-line loss: BCE + (1 − α)·Dice + α·clDice.

Arguments:
  • logits: (B, H, W) network outputs.
  • target: (B, H, W) masks in [0, 1] (soft at resampled edges).
  • known: Optional (B, H, W) or (H, W) weights in [0, 1]: where the masks say something (1) or nothing (0, the whole photo's side columns). Pixels of weight 0 count in neither term; None counts every pixel, exactly as before.
  • cldice: Weight of soft_cldice_loss() (CLDICE_WEIGHT when used); 0 returns exactly the loss of the named recipe.
  • iters: The soft skeleton's erosions (CL_ITERS).
Returns:

The loss, a scalar tensor.

def augment_pair( x, m, generator, params: SegParams = SegParams(size=256, encoder='resnet18', epochs=60, batch=8, lr_encoder=0.0001, lr_decoder=0.001, weight_decay=0.0001, crop=0.8, rotate=10.0, jitter=0.2, threshold=0.5, seed=0, depth=False, cldice=0.0, cl_iters=25), flip_p: float = 0.5, known=None): 
565def augment_pair(x, m, generator, params: SegParams = SegParams(), flip_p: float = 0.5, known=None):
566    """Random crop, rotation, mirror image and colour jitter, with the mask resampled alike.
567
568    The crop, rotation and mirror are one affine resampling per photo: a
569    fraction ``f`` of each side (``f² ∈ [crop, 1]`` of the area) at a random
570    position. The rotation is made in pixels, so it keeps angles in a
571    non-square frame too (in a square one the arithmetic is unchanged).
572
573    Args:
574        x: ``(B, C, H, W)`` floats in [0, 1] (C = 3, or 4 with the depth last,
575            which is not jittered).
576        m: ``(B, H, W)`` masks in [0, 1].
577        generator: A ``torch.Generator`` on ``x``'s device.
578        params: ``crop``, ``rotate`` and ``jitter``.
579        flip_p: Chance of the mirror image.
580        known: Optional ``(H, W)`` or ``(B, H, W)`` weights (:func:`seg_loss`),
581            resampled with the mask; pixels brought in from past the edge are
582            the edge's.
583
584    Returns:
585        ``(images, masks)``: normalised images and masks in [0, 1], same
586        shapes; with ``known``, ``(images, masks, known)``.
587    """
588    import torch
589    import torch.nn.functional as F
590
591    b, dev = x.shape[0], x.device
592    aspect = x.shape[-1] / x.shape[-2]                                       # width / height
593
594    def uniform(lo, hi):
595        """``b`` random numbers between ``lo`` and ``hi``, one per image."""
596        return lo + (hi - lo) * torch.rand(b, device=dev, generator=generator)
597
598    f = torch.sqrt(uniform(params.crop, 1.0))
599    a = torch.deg2rad(uniform(-params.rotate, params.rotate))
600    tx, ty = uniform(-1.0, 1.0) * (1 - f), uniform(-1.0, 1.0) * (1 - f)
601    sx = torch.where(torch.rand(b, device=dev, generator=generator) < flip_p, -f, f)
602    theta = torch.zeros(b, 2, 3, device=dev)
603    cos, sin = torch.cos(a), torch.sin(a)
604    # Rotation after the mirror and scale, in pixels: in the grid's [-1, 1] coordinates the off-diagonal
605    # terms carry the frame's aspect ratio (1 for a square frame).
606    theta[:, 0, 0], theta[:, 0, 1], theta[:, 0, 2] = cos * sx, -sin * f / aspect, tx
607    theta[:, 1, 0], theta[:, 1, 1], theta[:, 1, 2] = sin * sx * aspect, cos * f, ty
608    parts = [x, m.unsqueeze(1)]
609    if known is not None:
610        parts.append(known.expand(b, *m.shape[-2:]).unsqueeze(1).to(x.dtype))
611    both = torch.cat(parts, dim=1)
612    grid = F.affine_grid(theta, list(both.shape), align_corners=False)
613    both = F.grid_sample(both, grid, mode="bilinear", padding_mode="border", align_corners=False)
614    c = x.shape[1]
615    x, m = both[:, :c], both[:, c].clamp(0, 1)
616    if known is not None:
617        known = both[:, c + 1].clamp(0, 1)
618    j = params.jitter
619    if j > 0:
620        rgb, rest = x[:, :3], x[:, 3:]
621        rgb = rgb * uniform(1 - j, 1 + j).view(b, 1, 1, 1)                     # brightness
622        mean = rgb.mean(dim=(1, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
623        rgb = (rgb - mean) * uniform(1 - j, 1 + j).view(b, 1, 1, 1) + mean      # contrast
624        grey = (0.299 * rgb[:, 0] + 0.587 * rgb[:, 1] + 0.114 * rgb[:, 2]).unsqueeze(1)
625        rgb = grey + (rgb - grey) * uniform(1 - j, 1 + j).view(b, 1, 1, 1)      # saturation
626        x = torch.cat([rgb.clamp(0, 1), rest], dim=1)
627    return (normalise(x), m) if known is None else (normalise(x), m, known)

Random crop, rotation, mirror image and colour jitter, with the mask resampled alike.

The crop, rotation and mirror are one affine resampling per photo: a fraction f of each side (f² ∈ [crop, 1] of the area) at a random position. The rotation is made in pixels, so it keeps angles in a non-square frame too (in a square one the arithmetic is unchanged).

Arguments:
  • x: (B, C, H, W) floats in [0, 1] (C = 3, or 4 with the depth last, which is not jittered).
  • m: (B, H, W) masks in [0, 1].
  • generator: A torch.Generator on x's device.
  • params: crop, rotate and jitter.
  • flip_p: Chance of the mirror image.
  • known: Optional (H, W) or (B, H, W) weights (seg_loss()), resampled with the mask; pixels brought in from past the edge are the edge's.
Returns:

(images, masks): normalised images and masks in [0, 1], same shapes; with known, (images, masks, known).

def predict_masks(model, x_uint8, batch: int = 16) -> numpy.ndarray: 
634def predict_masks(model, x_uint8, batch: int = 16) -> np.ndarray:
635    """Branch probabilities, each the average of the photo's and (flipped back) its mirror image's.
636
637    Args:
638        model: The network.
639        x_uint8: ``(N, C, S, S)`` uint8 tensor on the model's device.
640        batch: Photos per forward pass.
641
642    Returns:
643        ``(N, H, W)`` float32 probabilities.
644    """
645    import torch
646
647    model.eval()
648    out = []
649    with torch.inference_mode():
650        for i in range(0, len(x_uint8), batch):
651            x = normalise(_float(x_uint8[i:i + batch]))
652            p = (torch.sigmoid(model(x)) + torch.sigmoid(model(x.flip(-1))).flip(-1)) / 2
653            out.append(p.float().cpu().numpy())
654    return np.concatenate(out) if out else np.zeros((0,) + tuple(x_uint8.shape[-2:]), np.float32)

Branch probabilities, each the average of the photo's and (flipped back) its mirror image's.

Arguments:
  • model: The network.
  • x_uint8: (N, C, S, S) uint8 tensor on the model's device.
  • batch: Photos per forward pass.
Returns:

(N, H, W) float32 probabilities.

def train_seg( model, x_uint8, m_uint8, epochs: int, params: SegParams, seed: int, val: tuple | None = None, on_epoch: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None) -> list[dict]: 
657def train_seg(model, x_uint8, m_uint8, epochs: int, params: SegParams, seed: int, val: tuple | None = None,
658              on_epoch: Callable[[dict], None] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
659    """Train ``model`` in place: AdamW with a cosine learning-rate decay over ``epochs``.
660
661    Args:
662        model: The :class:`UNet`, on its device.
663        x_uint8: ``(N, C, H, W)`` uint8 tensor of training photos on the device.
664        m_uint8: ``(N, H, W)`` uint8 tensor of their masks (0–255).
665        epochs: Epochs to train.
666        params: The recipe.
667        seed: Seed for the batch order and the augmentation.
668        val: Optional ``(x_uint8, m_uint8)`` held out; its loss (on the
669            mirror-averaged probabilities) is recorded after each epoch.
670        on_epoch: Called with each epoch's record.
671
672    Returns:
673        One record per epoch: ``{"epoch", "train_loss", "val_loss"}``.
674    """
675    import torch
676
677    dev = x_uint8.device
678    torch.manual_seed(seed)
679    km = known_map(params)                                  # None in the masks' own frame
680    known = None if km is None else torch.from_numpy(km).to(dev)
681    gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(seed)
682    # The pretrained encoder is only adjusted (a small learning rate); the new decoder learns from scratch.
683    enc, dec = model.groups()
684    opt = torch.optim.AdamW([{"params": enc, "lr": params.lr_encoder}, {"params": dec, "lr": params.lr_decoder}],
685                            weight_decay=params.weight_decay)
686    n = len(x_uint8)
687    steps = max(1, math.ceil(n / params.batch)) * max(1, epochs)
688    # The learning rate falls along half a cosine, from its full value at the first step to 0 at the last.
689    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(opt, lambda step: 0.5 * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * min(step, steps) / steps)))
690    extra = _loss_options(params)                           # the centre-line term, if the recipe has one
691    log = []
692    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
693        model.train()
694        order = torch.randperm(n, device=dev, generator=gen)    # a new order of the photos every epoch
695        total, count = 0.0, 0
696        for i in range(0, n, params.batch):
697            idx = order[i:i + params.batch]
698            if len(idx) < 2:                                   # batch norm needs two photos
699                continue
700            # Each batch is augmented afresh (crop, rotation, mirror, colour), the masks moved with their photos.
701            if known is None:
702                x, m = augment_pair(_float(x_uint8[idx]), _float(m_uint8[idx]), gen, params)
703                loss = seg_loss(model(x), m, **extra)
704            else:
705                x, m, k = augment_pair(_float(x_uint8[idx]), _float(m_uint8[idx]), gen, params, known=known)
706                loss = seg_loss(model(x), m, k, **extra)
707            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
708            loss.backward()
709            opt.step()
710            sched.step()
711            total, count = total + loss.item() * len(idx), count + len(idx)
712        record = {"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": total / max(count, 1), "val_loss": None}
713        if val is not None:
714            # The held-out loss is on the prediction as it will be made (mirror image averaged in), so the
715            # probabilities are turned back into logits for the same loss function.
716            p = torch.as_tensor(predict_masks(model, val[0])).clamp(1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
717            # The epochs are chosen by the recipe's own loss, centre-line term included. That term's soft
718            # skeleton takes seconds per epoch on a CPU, so it is computed where the network runs; the named
719            # recipe's loss stays on the CPU, exactly as before.
720            where = dev if extra else "cpu"
721            record["val_loss"] = float(seg_loss(torch.logit(p).to(where), _float(val[1]).to(where),
722                                               None if known is None else known.to(where), **extra))
723        log.append(record)
724        if on_epoch:
725            on_epoch(record)
726    return log

Train model in place: AdamW with a cosine learning-rate decay over epochs.

Arguments:
  • model: The UNet, on its device.
  • x_uint8: (N, C, H, W) uint8 tensor of training photos on the device.
  • m_uint8: (N, H, W) uint8 tensor of their masks (0–255).
  • epochs: Epochs to train.
  • params: The recipe.
  • seed: Seed for the batch order and the augmentation.
  • val: Optional (x_uint8, m_uint8) held out; its loss (on the mirror-averaged probabilities) is recorded after each epoch.
  • on_epoch: Called with each epoch's record.
Returns:

One record per epoch: {"epoch", "train_loss", "val_loss"}.

def cross_validate_seg( images: numpy.ndarray, masks: numpy.ndarray, has_mask: numpy.ndarray, rows: numpy.ndarray, fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]], params: SegParams = SegParams(size=256, encoder='resnet18', epochs=60, batch=8, lr_encoder=0.0001, lr_decoder=0.001, weight_decay=0.0001, crop=0.8, rotate=10.0, jitter=0.2, threshold=0.5, seed=0, depth=False, cldice=0.0, cl_iters=25), device: str | None = None, pretrained: bool = True, progress: Callable[[str], None] = <built-in function print>) -> dict: 
729def cross_validate_seg(images: np.ndarray, masks: np.ndarray, has_mask: np.ndarray, rows: np.ndarray,
730                       fold_rows: Sequence[Sequence[int]], params: SegParams = SegParams(), device: str | None = None,
731                       pretrained: bool = True, progress: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> dict:
732    """Train and predict every tree from the fold that holds its row out (see the module docstring).
733
734    Args:
735        images: ``(n, H, W, C)`` uint8 summer photos at ``params.size`` (:func:`load_frames`).
736        masks: ``(n, H, W)`` uint8 hand masks (0–255) in the same frame.
737        has_mask: ``(n,)`` bool; trees without a hand mask are predicted but never trained on.
738        rows: ``(n,)`` orchard rows.
739        fold_rows: Each fold's held-out rows (``splits.json``).
740        params: The recipe.
741        device: ``"cuda"``, ``"cpu"``, or None for the GPU if there is one.
742        pretrained: Start from the ImageNet weights (False: random, for tests).
743        progress: Where progress lines go.
744
745    Returns:
746        ``{"prob": (n, H, W) float32, "fold": (n,), "epochs": [...], "log": [...], "device": str}``.
747    """
748    import torch
749
750    device = device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
751    torch.manual_seed(params.seed)                          # the decoder's first weights
752    base = UNet(params.encoder, pretrained, channels=images.shape[3]).to(device)
753    start = copy.deepcopy(base.state_dict())
754    x_all = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(images.transpose(0, 3, 1, 2))).to(device)
755    m_all = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(masks)).to(device)
756    n = len(images)
757    prob, fold = np.full((n,) + images.shape[1:3], np.nan, np.float32), np.full(n, -1)
758    chosen, logs = [], []
759
760    def fresh():
761        """The network reset to its starting weights (one copy reused, to save memory)."""
762        base.load_state_dict(start)
763        return base
764
765    def take(sel):
766        """The photos and masks selected by the boolean ``sel``."""
767        idx = torch.from_numpy(np.nonzero(sel)[0]).to(device)
768        return x_all[idx], m_all[idx]
769
770    for i, held in enumerate(fold_rows):
771        # This fold's rows are predicted; the network trains on the other rows' trees that have a hand mask.
772        va = np.isin(rows, list(held))
773        tr = ~va & has_mask
774        if not va.any() or tr.sum() < 2:
775            continue
776        t0 = time.time()
777        # The number of epochs is chosen inside the training rows: the next fold's rows are held out, and the
778        # epoch with the lowest loss on them is kept. The fold's own rows play no part in the choice.
779        inner = _inner_rows(i, fold_rows, set(rows[tr].tolist()), rows[has_mask])
780        best = params.epochs
781        if inner is not None:
782            iv = tr & np.isin(rows, inner)
783            it = tr & ~iv
784            progress(f"Fold {i + 1}/{len(fold_rows)} (rows {sorted(map(int, held))}, {_n(va.sum(), 'tree')}): "
785                     f"choosing the epochs on rows {sorted(map(int, inner))} ({_n(iv.sum(), 'tree')})...")
786            log = train_seg(fresh(), *take(it), params.epochs, params, params.seed + 100 * i, val=take(iv),
787                            on_epoch=lambda r: (progress(f"  epoch {r['epoch']:3d}: train {r['train_loss']:.3f}, "
788                                                         f"held out {r['val_loss']:.3f}")
789                                                if r["epoch"] % 5 == 0 or r["epoch"] == 1 else None))
790            logs += [{"fold": i, "stage": "choose", **r} for r in log]
791            best = int(min(log, key=lambda r: r["val_loss"])["epoch"])
792            progress(f"  lowest held-out loss after {_n(best, 'epoch')}")
793        else:
794            progress(f"Fold {i + 1}/{len(fold_rows)}: no rows to hold out inside the training rows; "
795                     f"training for {_n(best, 'epoch')}")
796        # Then a fresh network trains on all the training rows for that many epochs and predicts the fold.
797        log = train_seg(fresh(), *take(tr), best, params, params.seed + 100 * i + 50)
798        logs += [{"fold": i, "stage": "final", **r} for r in log]
799        prob[va] = predict_masks(base, take(va)[0])
800        fold[va] = i
801        chosen.append({"fold": i, "epochs": best, "inner_rows": inner, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)})
802        progress(f"  trained on {_n(tr.sum(), 'tree')} for {_n(best, 'epoch')}; fold done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
803    return {"prob": prob, "fold": fold, "epochs": chosen, "log": logs, "device": device}

Train and predict every tree from the fold that holds its row out (see the module docstring).

Arguments:
  • images: (n, H, W, C) uint8 summer photos at params.size (load_frames()).
  • masks: (n, H, W) uint8 hand masks (0–255) in the same frame.
  • has_mask: (n,) bool; trees without a hand mask are predicted but never trained on.
  • rows: (n,) orchard rows.
  • fold_rows: Each fold's held-out rows (splits.json).
  • params: The recipe.
  • device: "cuda", "cpu", or None for the GPU if there is one.
  • pretrained: Start from the ImageNet weights (False: random, for tests).
  • progress: Where progress lines go.

def prob_frame(prob: numpy.ndarray, whole: bool = False) -> numpy.ndarray: 
810def prob_frame(prob: np.ndarray, whole: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
811    """Probabilities in the hand masks' 256x256 frame (float32), resized bilinearly.
812
813    Args:
814        prob: ``(S, S)`` probabilities in the masks' frame, or, with ``whole``,
815            ``(H, W)`` over the whole photo, whose centre columns
816            (:func:`known_columns`) are the masks' frame.
817        whole: ``prob`` covers the whole photo.
818
819    Returns:
820        ``(256, 256)`` float32 probabilities.
821    """
822    from PIL import Image
823
824    from treeskel.io import MASK_SHAPE
825
826    p = np.asarray(prob, np.float32)
827    if whole:
828        a, b = known_columns(p.shape[1])
829        p = np.ascontiguousarray(p[:, a:b])
830    if p.shape != MASK_SHAPE:
831        p = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(p).resize(MASK_SHAPE[::-1], Image.BILINEAR))
832    return p

def mask_scores(pred: numpy.ndarray, truth: numpy.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]: 
849def mask_scores(pred: np.ndarray, truth: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
850    """IoU, Dice, precision and recall of a predicted mask against a hand mask (NaN where undefined).
851
852    Args:
853        pred: Predicted boolean mask.
854        truth: Hand boolean mask, the same shape.
855
856    Returns:
857        ``{"iou", "dice", "precision", "recall"}``.
858    """
859    p, t = np.asarray(pred, bool), np.asarray(truth, bool)
860    tp = float((p & t).sum())
861    fp, fn = float((p & ~t).sum()), float((~p & t).sum())
862
863    def ratio(a, b):
864        """``a / b``, or NaN when ``b`` is 0."""
865        return a / b if b > 0 else float("nan")
866
867    return {"iou": ratio(tp, tp + fp + fn), "dice": ratio(2 * tp, 2 * tp + fp + fn),
868            "precision": ratio(tp, tp + fp), "recall": ratio(tp, tp + fn)}

JOIN_GAP = 19.3

Largest gap (mask px, nearest pixel centre to nearest pixel centre) that join_pieces() bridges: about a trunk's width. It is twice the development hand masks' median trunk radius at the fork (9.67 mask px as treeskel.shape.mask_branches() measures it, the distance from the centre line to the nearest background pixel; 448 trees), so up to about 18 background pixels, 36 px of the photo. Fixed from that geometry before any joined mask was scored (session 12); never tuned on the winter traces.

def join_pieces(mask: numpy.ndarray, gap: float = 19.3) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, int]: 
896def join_pieces(mask: np.ndarray, gap: float = JOIN_GAP) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
897    """Join the pieces of a broken predicted mask to its largest piece across gaps of at most ``gap``.
898
899    :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches` keeps only the largest piece, so a
900    leader cut from the trunk by a few pixels of leaves is lost, and with it
901    the fork. Here, starting from the largest piece, the nearest other piece
902    is joined if its nearest pixel is within ``gap`` of the joined mask, and
903    so on until none is (a piece may come within reach through one joined
904    before it). The join is a straight band between the two pieces' nearest
905    centre-line (skeleton) points, as wide as the narrower of the two near
906    there (the widest point of each centre line within ``gap`` of the join),
907    so the centre lines run on through it. Pixels are only added, and a mask
908    in one piece is returned unchanged.
909
910    Args:
911        mask: ``(H, W)`` bool predicted mask.
912        gap: Largest gap bridged (px, nearest pixel centre to nearest pixel
913            centre); 0 joins nothing.
914
915    Returns:
916        ``(joined mask, number of pieces joined)``.
917    """
918    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
919    from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
920
921    out = np.asarray(mask, bool).copy()
922    filled = ndi.binary_fill_holes(out)
923    lab, n = ndi.label(filled, np.ones((3, 3)))
924    if n < 2 or gap <= 0:
925        return out, 0
926    sizes = ndi.sum(filled, lab, range(1, n + 1))
927    first = int(np.argmax(sizes)) + 1
928    main = lab == first
929    rest = [k for k in range(1, n + 1) if k != first]
930    half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(filled)        # at a centre-line point: the piece's half-width
931    joined = 0
932    while rest:
933        to_main = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~main)         # distance to the nearest pixel of the joined mask
934        near = {k: float(to_main[lab == k].min()) for k in rest}
935        k = min(near, key=near.get)
936        if near[k] > gap:
937            break
938        piece = lab == k
939        # The two nearest centre-line points: one on the piece, one on the joined mask.
940        sk_main, sk_piece = skeletonize(main), skeletonize(piece)
941        d, (iy, ix) = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~sk_main, return_indices=True)
942        ys, xs = np.nonzero(sk_piece)
943        j = int(np.argmin(d[ys, xs]))
944        a, b = (int(ys[j]), int(xs[j])), (int(iy[ys[j], xs[j]]), int(ix[ys[j], xs[j]]))
945        width = min(_widest_near(half_width, sk_piece, a, gap), _widest_near(half_width, sk_main, b, gap))
946        band = _band(out.shape, a, b, width)
947        out |= band
948        main |= piece | band
949        rest.remove(k)
950        joined += 1
951    return out, joined

Join the pieces of a broken predicted mask to its largest piece across gaps of at most gap.

treeskel.shape.mask_branches() keeps only the largest piece, so a leader cut from the trunk by a few pixels of leaves is lost, and with it the fork. Here, starting from the largest piece, the nearest other piece is joined if its nearest pixel is within gap of the joined mask, and so on until none is (a piece may come within reach through one joined before it). The join is a straight band between the two pieces' nearest centre-line (skeleton) points, as wide as the narrower of the two near there (the widest point of each centre line within gap of the join), so the centre lines run on through it. Pixels are only added, and a mask in one piece is returned unchanged.

Arguments:
  • mask: (H, W) bool predicted mask.
  • gap: Largest gap bridged (px, nearest pixel centre to nearest pixel centre); 0 joins nothing.
Returns:

(joined mask, number of pieces joined).

GROW_LOWS = (0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05)

The lower thresholds choose_low() tries for grow_mask(), fixed before any run (session 12); 0.5 grows nothing.

def grow_mask( prob: numpy.ndarray, low: float, seed: numpy.ndarray | None = None, high: float = 0.5) -> numpy.ndarray: 
 977def grow_mask(prob: np.ndarray, low: float, seed: np.ndarray | None = None, high: float = 0.5) -> np.ndarray:
 978    """Hysteresis thresholding: the confident mask plus every less sure pixel connected to it.
 979
 980    Where leaves hide a leader, the U-Net's probability often fades below the
 981    threshold before the leader ends, so the mask stops short or breaks. Here
 982    pixels above ``low`` are kept wherever they connect (8-connected, through
 983    other such pixels) to the confident mask; faint patches that touch no
 984    confident pixel stay out. It uses only the network's own output.
 985
 986    Args:
 987        prob: ``(H, W)`` probabilities.
 988        low: Lower threshold; ``low >= high`` grows nothing.
 989        seed: The confident mask (default ``prob > high``); pass the saved
 990            mask so that it is kept exactly.
 991        high: The threshold the mask was made with.
 992
 993    Returns:
 994        ``(H, W)`` bool: ``seed`` and the grown pixels.
 995    """
 996    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
 997
 998    p = np.asarray(prob, np.float32)
 999    seed = p > high if seed is None else np.asarray(seed, bool)
1000    candidates = seed | (p > low)
1001    lab, n = ndi.label(candidates, np.ones((3, 3)))
1002    keep = np.zeros(n + 1, bool)
1003    keep[np.unique(lab[seed])] = True
1004    keep[0] = False
1005    return keep[lab]

Hysteresis thresholding: the confident mask plus every less sure pixel connected to it.

Where leaves hide a leader, the U-Net's probability often fades below the threshold before the leader ends, so the mask stops short or breaks. Here pixels above low are kept wherever they connect (8-connected, through other such pixels) to the confident mask; faint patches that touch no confident pixel stay out. It uses only the network's own output.

Arguments:
  • prob: (H, W) probabilities.
  • low: Lower threshold; low >= high grows nothing.
  • seed: The confident mask (default prob > high); pass the saved mask so that it is kept exactly.
  • high: The threshold the mask was made with.
Returns:

(H, W) bool: seed and the grown pixels.

def cl_dice(pred: numpy.ndarray, truth: numpy.ndarray) -> float: 
1008def cl_dice(pred: np.ndarray, truth: np.ndarray) -> float:
1009    """Centre-line Dice (Shit et al., 2021): how well two masks' centre lines lie in each other.
1010
1011    The harmonic mean of the fraction of the prediction's centre line inside
1012    the truth (topology precision) and of the truth's centre line inside the
1013    prediction (topology sensitivity). A leader that stops short or breaks
1014    loses sensitivity; growth into leaves beside the branch loses precision.
1015    Unlike the pixel Dice, it is not dominated by the wide trunk. NaN if
1016    either mask is empty.
1017
1018    Args:
1019        pred: Predicted boolean mask.
1020        truth: Hand boolean mask, the same shape.
1021
1022    Returns:
1023        The centre-line Dice in [0, 1], or NaN.
1024    """
1025    from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
1026
1027    p, t = np.asarray(pred, bool), np.asarray(truth, bool)
1028    sp, st = skeletonize(p), skeletonize(t)
1029    if not sp.any() or not st.any():
1030        return float("nan")
1031    prec, sens = (sp & t).sum() / sp.sum(), (st & p).sum() / st.sum()
1032    return float(2 * prec * sens / (prec + sens)) if prec + sens > 0 else 0.0

Centre-line Dice (Shit et al., 2021): how well two masks' centre lines lie in each other.

The harmonic mean of the fraction of the prediction's centre line inside the truth (topology precision) and of the truth's centre line inside the prediction (topology sensitivity). A leader that stops short or breaks loses sensitivity; growth into leaves beside the branch loses precision. Unlike the pixel Dice, it is not dominated by the wide trunk. NaN if either mask is empty.

Arguments:
  • pred: Predicted boolean mask.
  • truth: Hand boolean mask, the same shape.
Returns:

The centre-line Dice in [0, 1], or NaN.

def choose_low( probs: dict[str, numpy.ndarray], seeds: dict[str, numpy.ndarray], hands: dict[str, numpy.ndarray], lows: Sequence[float] = (0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05), gap: float = 19.3, progress: Callable[[str], None] = <built-in function print>) -> tuple[float, dict[str, float]]: 
1035def choose_low(probs: dict[str, np.ndarray], seeds: dict[str, np.ndarray], hands: dict[str, np.ndarray],
1036               lows: Sequence[float] = GROW_LOWS, gap: float = JOIN_GAP,
1037               progress: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> tuple[float, dict[str, float]]:
1038    """The lower threshold of :func:`grow_mask` whose masks, grown and joined, best match the hand masks'
1039    centre lines (mean :func:`cl_dice` over the trees with a hand mask). The winter traces play no part.
1040
1041    Args:
1042        probs: ``{tree: (256, 256) probabilities}`` in the masks' frame, each from the fold that held it out.
1043        seeds: ``{tree: the saved mask}``.
1044        hands: ``{tree: its (lined-up) hand mask}``.
1045        lows: The thresholds tried; on a tie the higher (less growth) wins.
1046        gap: The joining gap applied after growing, as in the scored masks.
1047        progress: Prints a progress line.
1048
1049    Returns:
1050        ``(chosen low, {str(low): mean clDice})``.
1051    """
1052    trees = [t for t in probs if t in hands]
1053    table = {}
1054    for low in lows:
1055        vals = [cl_dice(join_pieces(grow_mask(probs[t], low, seeds[t]), gap)[0], hands[t]) for t in trees]
1056        table[f"{low:g}"] = float(np.nanmean(vals))
1057        progress(f"  lower threshold {low:<4g}: mean clDice {table[f'{low:g}']:.4f} ({len(trees)} trees)")
1058    best = max(lows, key=lambda v: (round(table[f"{v:g}"], 6), v))
1059    return float(best), table

CONTINUE_CONE = 25.0

Largest angle (degrees) between a short leader's direction at its tip and a piece that continue_leaders() joins to it: the development hand masks' leaders turn by at most 24.8 degrees between the two halves of the fitted stretch in 95% of cases (896 leaders), so a piece further off that line is more likely another branch than the same leader. Fixed before any continued mask was scored (session 12); never tuned on the winter traces.

def continue_leaders( mask: numpy.ndarray, cone: float = 25.0, params: treeskel.shape.ShapeParams = ShapeParams(start=1.5, reach=16.0, trunk_reach=4.0, min_trunk=10.0, min_points=10, unit=16.5), rounds: int = 5) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, int]: 
1110def continue_leaders(mask: np.ndarray, cone: float = CONTINUE_CONE, params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams(),
1111                     rounds: int = 5) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
1112    """Join pieces lying on a short leader's way on, then keep only the trunk and the two leaders.
1113
1114    The student's idea (session 12): where leaves hide a leader, the mask
1115    often stops, and a piece of the same leader lies further along its line,
1116    too far for :func:`join_pieces`. Here, for each leader shorter than the
1117    stretch the angles are fitted over (``params.reach`` units at
1118    :data:`treeskel.shape.MASK_ZOOM`), the pieces of the mask not joined to
1119    the tree are searched: one is joined if some pixel of it lies within the
1120    part of the stretch still missing (``reach`` minus the leader's length)
1121    of the tip and within ``cone`` degrees of the leader's direction at its
1122    tip (a line through its last ``params.trunk_reach`` units, the length of
1123    the trunk's axis), and it has at least ``params.min_points`` px of
1124    centre line. The nearest such piece is joined by a band from the tip to
1125    its nearest centre-line point, as :func:`join_pieces` joins; the leaders
1126    are found again and the search repeats (a chain of pieces), up to
1127    ``rounds`` times. Finally the mask is cut down to the trunk and the two
1128    leaders (:func:`prune_to_branches`).
1129
1130    Args:
1131        mask: ``(256, 256)`` bool mask, already joined (:func:`join_pieces`).
1132        cone: :data:`CONTINUE_CONE`.
1133        params: The shape measures' stretch.
1134        rounds: Most joins per leader search.
1135
1136    Returns:
1137        ``(the trunk and leaders, pieces joined)``; a mask with no fork is returned unchanged.
1138    """
1139    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
1140    from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
1141
1142    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1143    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px
1144
1145    out = np.asarray(mask, bool).copy()
1146    unit = unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1147    reach, tip_len = params.reach * unit, params.trunk_reach * unit
1148    joined = 0
1149    br = mask_branches(out)
1150    if br is None:
1151        return out, 0
1152    for _ in range(rounds):
1153        # The mask's pieces; the tree is the piece holding the trunk's top.
1154        filled = ndi.binary_fill_holes(out)
1155        lab, n = ndi.label(filled, np.ones((3, 3)))
1156        tree = lab[tuple(br["trunk"][-1])]
1157        half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(filled)
1158        best = None                                         # (distance, side, piece label)
1159        for side in ("left", "right"):
1160            path = br[side]
1161            length = float(arc_length(path)[-1]) if len(path) > 1 else 0.0
1162            if length >= reach or len(path) < 2:
1163                continue
1164            tip, d = np.asarray(path[-1], float), _tip_direction(path, tip_len)
1165            # A candidate piece has a pixel within the missing stretch of the tip and inside the cone
1166            # around the leader's direction (cosine test: v . d >= |v| cos(cone)).
1167            for k in range(1, n + 1):
1168                if k == tree:
1169                    continue
1170                ys, xs = np.nonzero(lab == k)
1171                v = np.stack([ys, xs], 1) - tip
1172                dist = np.hypot(v[:, 0], v[:, 1])
1173                ok = (dist <= reach - length) & (v @ d >= np.cos(np.radians(cone)) * dist)
1174                if not ok.any() or skeletonize(lab == k).sum() < params.min_points:
1175                    continue
1176                if best is None or dist[ok].min() < best[0]:
1177                    best = (float(dist[ok].min()), side, k)
1178        if best is None:
1179            break
1180        # Join the nearest candidate: a band from the leader's tip to the piece's nearest centre-line point,
1181        # as wide as the narrower of the two ends (as join_pieces joins).
1182        _, side, k = best
1183        piece = lab == k
1184        sk_piece = skeletonize(piece)
1185        ys, xs = np.nonzero(sk_piece)
1186        tip = tuple(int(v) for v in br[side][-1])
1187        j = int(np.argmin(np.hypot(ys - tip[0], xs - tip[1])))
1188        b = (int(ys[j]), int(xs[j]))
1189        tree_line = np.zeros_like(out)
1190        tree_line[tuple(np.asarray(br[side]).T)] = True
1191        width = min(_widest_near(half_width, sk_piece, b, JOIN_GAP), _widest_near(half_width, tree_line, tip, JOIN_GAP))
1192        out |= _band(out.shape, tip, b, width)
1193        joined += 1
1194        found = mask_branches(out)                          # the leaders again, for the next round
1195        if found is None:                                   # cannot happen when joining to the tree; be safe
1196            break
1197        br = found
1198    return prune_to_branches(out, br), joined

Join pieces lying on a short leader's way on, then keep only the trunk and the two leaders.

The student's idea (session 12): where leaves hide a leader, the mask often stops, and a piece of the same leader lies further along its line, too far for join_pieces(). Here, for each leader shorter than the stretch the angles are fitted over (params.reach units at treeskel.shape.MASK_ZOOM), the pieces of the mask not joined to the tree are searched: one is joined if some pixel of it lies within the part of the stretch still missing (reach minus the leader's length) of the tip and within cone degrees of the leader's direction at its tip (a line through its last params.trunk_reach units, the length of the trunk's axis), and it has at least params.min_points px of centre line. The nearest such piece is joined by a band from the tip to its nearest centre-line point, as join_pieces() joins; the leaders are found again and the search repeats (a chain of pieces), up to rounds times. Finally the mask is cut down to the trunk and the two leaders (prune_to_branches()).

Arguments:
  • mask: (256, 256) bool mask, already joined (join_pieces()).
  • cone: CONTINUE_CONE.
  • params: The shape measures' stretch.
  • rounds: Most joins per leader search.
Returns:

(the trunk and leaders, pieces joined); a mask with no fork is returned unchanged.

def prune_to_branches(mask: numpy.ndarray, br: dict) -> numpy.ndarray: 
1201def prune_to_branches(mask: np.ndarray, br: dict) -> np.ndarray:
1202    """The mask cut down to the trunk and the two leaders: its pixels within each path point's own half-width
1203    (the distance to the mask's edge there) of the paths :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches` found.
1204
1205    Args:
1206        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
1207        br: Its branches, from :func:`treeskel.shape.mask_branches`.
1208
1209    Returns:
1210        The pruned boolean mask.
1211    """
1212    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
1213
1214    filled = ndi.binary_fill_holes(np.asarray(mask, bool))
1215    half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(filled)
1216    pts = np.concatenate([np.asarray(br[p]).reshape(-1, 2) for p in ("trunk", "left", "right")])
1217    seeds = np.zeros(filled.shape, bool)
1218    seeds[pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1]] = True
1219    dist, (iy, ix) = ndi.distance_transform_edt(~seeds, return_indices=True)
1220    return filled & (dist < half_width[iy, ix])

The mask cut down to the trunk and the two leaders: its pixels within each path point's own half-width (the distance to the mask's edge there) of the paths treeskel.shape.mask_branches() found.

Arguments:

  • br: Its branches, from treeskel.shape.mask_branches().

The pruned boolean mask.

COMPLETE_FRACTIONS = (0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95)

Where completion_samples() cuts complete leaders (fractions of the fitted stretch, 0.40-0.95): the lengths short predicted leaders stop at (the re-run's joined masks: median 0.75 of the stretch, quartiles 0.54-0.89; the named run's: 0.69, 0.42-0.88).

def completion_samples( masks: dict[str, numpy.ndarray], params: treeskel.shape.ShapeParams = ShapeParams(start=1.5, reach=16.0, trunk_reach=4.0, min_trunk=10.0, min_points=10, unit=16.5), fractions: Sequence[float] = (0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95)) -> numpy.ndarray: 
1246def completion_samples(masks: dict[str, np.ndarray], params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams(),
1247                       fractions: Sequence[float] = COMPLETE_FRACTIONS) -> np.ndarray:
1248    """Complete leaders cut short on purpose: ``(n, 4)`` rows of ``(missing fraction g, outward line of the
1249    cut leader, its bend, outward line of the whole)``, for :func:`fit_completion`.
1250
1251    Every leader of ``masks`` that spans the whole fitted stretch is cut at each of ``fractions`` of it.
1252
1253    Args:
1254        masks: 256x256 boolean masks per tree id.
1255        params: The shape measures' settings.
1256        fractions: The fractions of the stretch cut off.
1257
1258    Returns:
1259        The samples.
1260    """
1261    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1262    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px
1263
1264    reach = params.reach * unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1265    rows = []
1266    for m in masks.values():
1267        _, br = mask_shape(m, params)
1268        if br is None:
1269            continue
1270        for side in ("left", "right"):
1271            s = arc_length(br[side]) if len(br[side]) > 1 else np.zeros(1)
1272            if s[-1] < reach:
1273                continue
1274            whole, _ = _outward(br[side], side, params)
1275            for f in fractions:
1276                cut, bend = _outward(br[side][s <= f * reach], side, params)
1277                if np.isfinite(cut) and np.isfinite(whole):
1278                    rows.append((1 - f, cut, bend, whole))
1279    return np.array(rows, float).reshape(-1, 4)

Complete leaders cut short on purpose: (n, 4) rows of (missing fraction g, outward line of the cut leader, its bend, outward line of the whole), for fit_completion().

Every leader of masks that spans the whole fitted stretch is cut at each of fractions of it.

Arguments:
  • masks: 256x256 boolean masks per tree id.
  • params: The shape measures' settings.
  • fractions: The fractions of the stretch cut off.
Returns:

The samples.

def fit_completion(samples: numpy.ndarray) -> numpy.ndarray: 
1282def fit_completion(samples: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
1283    """Least squares for the change of a leader's line over its missing part:
1284    ``whole − cut = a·g + c·g·bend`` (``g`` the missing fraction; a missing bend counts as 0).
1285
1286    Args:
1287        samples: From :func:`completion_samples`.
1288
1289    Returns:
1290        ``(a, c)``: the change (degrees) per unit of missing fraction, and per unit of missing fraction
1291        and bend.
1292    """
1293    g, cut, bend, whole = samples.T
1294    x = np.stack([g, g * np.nan_to_num(bend)], 1)
1295    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(x, whole - cut, rcond=None)
1296    return coef

Least squares for the change of a leader's line over its missing part: whole − cut = a·g + c·g·bend (g the missing fraction; a missing bend counts as 0).

def complete_measures( mask: numpy.ndarray, coef: Sequence[float], params: treeskel.shape.ShapeParams = ShapeParams(start=1.5, reach=16.0, trunk_reach=4.0, min_trunk=10.0, min_points=10, unit=16.5)) -> tuple[dict[str, float], int]: 
1299def complete_measures(mask: np.ndarray, coef: Sequence[float], params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams()
1300                      ) -> tuple[dict[str, float], int]:
1301    """:func:`mask_shape` with each short leader's line predicted over the whole fitted stretch.
1302
1303    A leader shorter than the stretch has its line from the vertical moved
1304    by :func:`fit_completion`'s model (``a·g + c·g·bend``, outwards); the
1305    measures built on the leader lines (the V opening, the angles from the
1306    trunk, the V's lean, the tilts) follow. The bends stay as measured.
1307
1308    Args:
1309        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
1310        coef: ``(a, c)`` from :func:`fit_completion`.
1311        params: The shape measures' settings.
1312
1313    Returns:
1314        ``(measures, leaders completed)``.
1315    """
1316    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1317    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px, wrap
1318
1319    m, br = mask_shape(mask, params)
1320    if br is None:
1321        return m, 0
1322    reach = params.reach * unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1323    a, c = coef
1324    tilts, done = {}, 0
1325    for side in ("left", "right"):
1326        tilts[side] = m[f"{side}_tilt"]
1327        length = float(arc_length(br[side])[-1]) if len(br[side]) > 1 else 0.0
1328        if length >= reach or not np.isfinite(tilts[side]):
1329            continue
1330        g = 1 - length / reach
1331        _, bend = _outward(br[side], side, params)
1332        shift = a * g + c * g * (0.0 if not np.isfinite(bend) else bend)
1333        tilts[side] += shift if side == "right" else -shift
1334        done += 1
1335    if not done:
1336        return m, 0
1337    out = dict(m)
1338    out["left_tilt"], out["right_tilt"] = tilts["left"], tilts["right"]
1339    trunk = m["trunk_tilt"]
1340    if np.isfinite(tilts["left"]) and np.isfinite(tilts["right"]):
1341        out["v_opening"] = wrap(tilts["right"] - tilts["left"])
1342        out["lean_v"] = (tilts["left"] + tilts["right"]) / 2
1343        if np.isfinite(trunk):
1344            out["lean"] = wrap(out["lean_v"] - trunk)
1345    if np.isfinite(trunk):
1346        out["left_angle"] = wrap(trunk - tilts["left"]) if np.isfinite(tilts["left"]) else float("nan")
1347        out["right_angle"] = wrap(tilts["right"] - trunk) if np.isfinite(tilts["right"]) else float("nan")
1348    return out, done

mask_shape() with each short leader's line predicted over the whole fitted stretch.

A leader shorter than the stretch has its line from the vertical moved by fit_completion()'s model (a·g + c·g·bend, outwards); the measures built on the leader lines (the V opening, the angles from the trunk, the V's lean, the tilts) follow. The bends stay as measured.

Arguments:
  • mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
  • coef: (a, c) from fit_completion().
  • params: The shape measures' settings.
Returns:

(measures, leaders completed).

def draw_completion( mask: numpy.ndarray, coef: Sequence[float], params: treeskel.shape.ShapeParams = ShapeParams(start=1.5, reach=16.0, trunk_reach=4.0, min_trunk=10.0, min_points=10, unit=16.5)) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray]: 
1351def draw_completion(mask: np.ndarray, coef: Sequence[float], params: ShapeParams = ShapeParams()
1352                    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
1353    """The mask with each short leader drawn on over the missing part of the stretch, as :func:`complete_measures`
1354    predicts it: from the tip, along the leader's predicted line, as wide as the leader near its tip.
1355
1356    For showing the prediction (a leader that goes on through the leaves, not a stub); the scores come
1357    from :func:`complete_measures`.
1358
1359    Args:
1360        mask: A 256x256 boolean mask.
1361        coef: ``(a, c)`` from :func:`fit_completion`.
1362        params: The shape measures' settings.
1363
1364    Returns:
1365        ``(mask with the continuations, the continuations alone)``.
1366    """
1367    from scipy import ndimage as ndi
1368
1369    from treeskel.guided_gt import arc_length
1370    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM, unit_px
1371
1372    out = np.asarray(mask, bool).copy()
1373    added = np.zeros_like(out)
1374    m, br = mask_shape(out, params)
1375    if br is None:
1376        return out, added
1377    reach = params.reach * unit_px(0.0, params, MASK_ZOOM)
1378    a, c = coef
1379    half_width = ndi.distance_transform_edt(ndi.binary_fill_holes(out))
1380    h, w = out.shape
1381    for side in ("left", "right"):
1382        path = np.asarray(br[side])
1383        length = float(arc_length(path)[-1]) if len(path) > 1 else 0.0
1384        if length >= reach or not np.isfinite(m[f"{side}_tilt"]):
1385            continue
1386        g = 1 - length / reach
1387        line, bend = _outward(path, side, params)
1388        whole = line + a * g + c * g * (0.0 if not np.isfinite(bend) else bend)
1389        angle = np.radians(whole if side == "right" else -whole)
1390        d = np.array([-np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)])     # (row, col), upwards
1391        tip = path[-1].astype(float)
1392        steps = np.arange(0.0, reach - length, 0.5)
1393        pts = tip + steps[:, None] * d
1394        inside = (pts[:, 0] >= 0) & (pts[:, 0] <= h - 1) & (pts[:, 1] >= 0) & (pts[:, 1] <= w - 1)
1395        if not inside.any():
1396            continue
1397        end = tuple(int(round(v)) for v in pts[np.nonzero(inside)[0][-1]])
1398        leader = np.zeros_like(out)
1399        leader[path[:, 0], path[:, 1]] = True
1400        width = _widest_near(half_width, leader, tuple(int(v) for v in tip), JOIN_GAP)
1401        added |= _band(out.shape, tuple(int(v) for v in tip), end, width) & ~out
1402    return out | added, added

def fill_failures(pred: numpy.ndarray, mean: numpy.ndarray) -> numpy.ndarray: 
1405def fill_failures(pred: np.ndarray, mean: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
1406    """Predictions with each tree whose mask gave no shape at all replaced by the mean shape.
1407
1408    A tree whose predicted mask has a fork but, say, no trunk axis keeps NaN on
1409    the trunk measures, as the winter trace and the hand mask of such a tree do.
1410
1411    Args:
1412        pred: ``(n, measures)`` predictions, NaN where a mask gave none.
1413        mean: ``(n, measures)``: each tree's fold's mean shape.
1414
1415    Returns:
1416        The filled ``(n, measures)`` predictions.
1417    """
1418    out = pred.copy()
1419    failed = ~np.isfinite(pred).any(axis=1)
1420    out[failed] = mean[failed]
1421    return out

def compare_with( seg: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]], other: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]], names: Sequence[str] = ('v_opening', 'left_angle', 'right_angle', 'lean', 'left_bend', 'right_bend', 'trunk_tilt', 'left_tilt', 'right_tilt', 'lean_v')) -> dict: 
1424def compare_with(seg: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]], other: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]],
1425                 names: Sequence[str] = MEASURES) -> dict:
1426    """The segmentation against another model, tree by tree, on the trees both predict.
1427
1428    Args:
1429        seg: The segmentation's ``{(tree, measure): (winter, prediction)}`` (:func:`read_predictions`).
1430        other: The other model's, in the same form.
1431        names: The measures compared.
1432
1433    Returns:
1434        ``{measure: {"n", "closer", "wilcoxon_p", "mae_seg", "mae_other"}}``: the fraction of trees the
1435        segmentation predicts more closely, and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the paired absolute errors.
1436    """
1437    from scipy import stats
1438
1439    out = {}
1440    for k in names:
1441        keys = [key for key in seg if key[1] == k and key in other]
1442        if len(keys) < 3:
1443            continue
1444        e_s = np.array([abs(seg[key][1] - seg[key][0]) for key in keys])
1445        e_o = np.array([abs(other[key][1] - other[key][0]) for key in keys])
1446        diff = e_o - e_s
1447        out[k] = {"n": len(keys), "closer": float(np.mean(diff > 0)),
1448                  "wilcoxon_p": float(stats.wilcoxon(diff).pvalue) if np.any(diff != 0) else 1.0,
1449                  "mae_seg": float(e_s.mean()), "mae_other": float(e_o.mean())}
1450    return out

def load_frames( records: dict, ids: Sequence[str], size: int | tuple[int, int], depth: bool = False, progress: Callable[[str], None] = <built-in function print>, overlays: dict | None = None) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray]: 
1502def load_frames(records: dict, ids: Sequence[str], size: int | tuple[int, int], depth: bool = False,
1503                progress: Callable[[str], None] = print,
1504                overlays: dict | None = None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
1505    """The summer photos and hand masks of ``ids``: in the masks' frame (centre 480x480) at ``size`` x ``size``,
1506    or, for ``size = (height, width)``, the whole photo at that size with each mask on its centre columns
1507    (:func:`mask_to_photo`).
1508
1509    With ``overlays`` (the mask line-up file), each mask is moved onto its photo
1510    (:func:`hand_mask`), and trees not lined up count as having none.
1511
1512    Args:
1513        records: Tree records by id.
1514        ids: The trees to load.
1515        size: Square side (the masks' frame), or ``(height, width)`` (the whole photo).
1516        depth: Add the summer depth as a fourth channel.
1517        progress: Prints a progress line.
1518        overlays: The mask line-ups; None for the masks as drawn.
1519
1520    Returns:
1521        ``(images, masks, has_mask)``: ``(n, H, W, 3 or 4)`` uint8 (depth
1522        last, nearest-neighbour so no-reading zeros are not blended),
1523        ``(n, H, W)`` uint8 masks (0–255, bilinear, so soft at the edges;
1524        zero where there is none, and on a whole photo's side columns) and ``(n,)`` bool.
1525    """
1526    from PIL import Image
1527
1528    from treeskel.io import CROP_COLS, load_tree
1529
1530    whole = not isinstance(size, int)
1531    h, w = (int(size[0]), int(size[1])) if whole else (size, size)
1532    images = np.zeros((len(ids), h, w, 4 if depth else 3), np.uint8)
1533    masks = np.zeros((len(ids), h, w), np.uint8)
1534    has = np.zeros(len(ids), bool)
1535    step = max(1, len(ids) // 10)
1536    for i, t in enumerate(ids):
1537        summer = load_tree(records[t], "summer")
1538        crop = slice(0, None) if whole else slice(CROP_COLS[0], CROP_COLS[1])
1539        images[i, ..., :3] = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(np.ascontiguousarray(summer["rgb"][:, crop]))
1540                                        .resize((w, h), Image.BILINEAR))
1541        if depth:
1542            images[i, ..., 3] = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(np.ascontiguousarray(summer["depth"][:, crop]))
1543                                           .resize((w, h), Image.NEAREST))
1544        hm = hand_mask(records[t], overlays)
1545        if hm is not None:
1546            masks[i] = (mask_to_photo(hm, (h, w)) if whole else
1547                        np.asarray(Image.fromarray(hm.astype(np.uint8) * 255).resize((w, h), Image.BILINEAR)))
1548            has[i] = True
1549        if (i + 1) % step == 0 or i + 1 == len(ids):
1550            progress(f"  {i + 1}/{len(ids)} photos loaded")
1551    return images, masks, has

The summer photos and hand masks of ids: in the masks' frame (centre 480x480) at size x size, or, for size = (height, width), the whole photo at that size with each mask on its centre columns (mask_to_photo()).

With overlays (the mask line-up file), each mask is moved onto its photo (hand_mask()), and trees not lined up count as having none.

Arguments:

def example_trees(dice: dict[str, float], k: int = 6) -> list[str]: 
1581def example_trees(dice: dict[str, float], k: int = 6) -> list[str]:
1582    """Trees at evenly spaced quantiles of the Dice score, worst to best, so the figure shows the range
1583    rather than the best cases.
1584
1585    Args:
1586        dice: Dice per tree id.
1587        k: Trees wanted.
1588
1589    Returns:
1590        Tree ids; empty if no tree has a finite score.
1591    """
1592    ranked = sorted((v, t) for t, v in dice.items() if np.isfinite(v))
1593    if not ranked:
1594        return []
1595    picks = np.unique(np.round(np.linspace(0, len(ranked) - 1, min(k, len(ranked)))).astype(int))
1596    return [ranked[i][1] for i in picks]

def draw_example( rec, pred: numpy.ndarray, trace: dict | None, label: str, scale: float = 0.5, overlays: dict | None = None, continuation: numpy.ndarray | None = None): 
1599def draw_example(rec, pred: np.ndarray, trace: dict | None, label: str, scale: float = 0.5,
1600                 overlays: dict | None = None, continuation: np.ndarray | None = None):
1601    """One tree as a row of three: the winter trace, the hand mask and the predicted mask, each with the
1602    lines :func:`treeskel.shape.shape_measures` fits (PIL image, resized by ``scale``, then labelled). With
1603    ``overlays``, the hand mask is shown lined up (:func:`hand_mask`); ``continuation`` (from
1604    :func:`draw_completion`) is shown in orange on the predicted mask.
1605
1606    Args:
1607        rec: The tree's record.
1608        pred: Its predicted 256x256 boolean mask.
1609        trace: Its winter trace (``{"trunk", "left", "right"}``), or None.
1610        label: Text written on the row.
1611        scale: Size relative to the photos.
1612        overlays: The mask line-ups; None for the mask as drawn.
1613        continuation: Pixels drawn on by :func:`draw_completion`, or None.
1614
1615    Returns:
1616        The row as a PIL image.
1617    """
1618    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
1619
1620    from treeskel.io import load_tree, mask_to_image_frame
1621    from treeskel.shape import MASK_ZOOM as ZOOM, draw_shape, fitted_lines, mask_to_image
1622
1623    params = ShapeParams()
1624    s = load_tree(rec, "summer")["rgb"]
1625
1626    def on_summer(mask, name, colour, extra=None):
1627        """The summer photo with ``mask`` (``extra`` in orange) shaded and its lines drawn, and its label."""
1628        img = s.copy()
1629        full, _ = mask_to_image_frame(np.asarray(mask, bool))
1630        img[full] = (0.45 * img[full] + 0.55 * np.array(colour)).astype(np.uint8)
1631        if extra is not None and np.any(extra):
1632            more, _ = mask_to_image_frame(np.asarray(extra, bool))
1633            img[more] = (0.3 * img[more] + 0.7 * np.array((255, 150, 0))).astype(np.uint8)
1634        br = mask_branches(mask)
1635        if br is None:
1636            return draw_shape(img, (), {}), f"{name}: no fork found"
1637        lines = {k: tuple(mask_to_image(np.array(v)))
1638                 for k, v in fitted_lines(br["trunk"], br["left"], br["right"], br["fork_radius"], params, ZOOM).items()}
1639        return draw_shape(img, [mask_to_image(br[p]) for p in ("trunk", "left", "right")], lines), name
1640
1641    tiles = []                                             # (image, label)
1642    if trace is not None:
1643        w = load_tree(rec, "winter")["rgb"]
1644        lines = fitted_lines(trace["trunk"], trace["left"], trace["right"], trace["fork_radius"], params)
1645        tiles.append((draw_shape(w, (trace["trunk"], trace["left"], trace["right"]), lines), f"{label}: winter trace"))
1646    hand = hand_mask(rec, overlays)
1647    tiles.append(on_summer(hand, "hand mask, lined up" if overlays is not None else "hand mask", (60, 120, 255))
1648                 if hand is not None else (draw_shape(s, (), {}), "no hand mask used"))
1649    shown = continuation is not None and np.any(continuation)
1650    tiles.append(on_summer(pred, "predicted mask" + (" (orange: predicted on)" if shown else ""), (0, 200, 0),
1651                           continuation))
1652    size = (round(tiles[0][0].width * scale), round(tiles[0][0].height * scale))
1653    out = Image.new("RGB", (size[0] * len(tiles), size[1]))
1654    dr = ImageDraw.Draw(out)
1655    font = ImageFont.load_default(size=14)
1656    for i, (im, text) in enumerate(tiles):
1657        out.paste(im.resize(size, Image.BILINEAR), (i * size[0], 0))
1658        dr.text((i * size[0] + 6, 5), text, fill=(255, 255, 0), font=font, stroke_width=2, stroke_fill=(0, 0, 0))
1659    return out

One tree as a row of three: the winter trace, the hand mask and the predicted mask, each with the lines treeskel.shape.shape_measures() fits (PIL image, resized by scale, then labelled). With overlays, the hand mask is shown lined up (hand_mask()); continuation (from draw_completion()) is shown in orange on the predicted mask.

def against_runs( out: pathlib._local.Path, others: Sequence[tuple[str, str]] = (('shape_cnn', 'cnn fine-tuned'), ('shape_cnn_480x640', 'cnn fine-tuned'), ('segment', 'segmentation'), ('segment_lined_up', 'segmentation'), ('segment_lined_up_joined', 'segmentation'))) -> dict:
